docs.title: Unreleased
docs.text:
• Documentation site rebuilt with MkDocs Material from docs_src/, with pages on the system, scenarios, simulators, experiments, deployment and reference.
  • bikeped.scenarios: scenario registry with the paper's 24 conformance scenarios unchanged, an extended suite of 41 scenarios, a stress suite of 8 dense scenes, six seeded generator families and a command line (python -m bikeped.scenarios).
  • bikeped.sim: CARLA renderer for Unreal Engine 4 (CARLA 0.9.14 to 0.9.16) and Unreal Engine 5 (CARLA 0.10.0) with six camera views, the deployed fisheye rendered from cube faces, weather and ambient traffic presets, per-frame ground truth and COCO/YOLO export. It replaces the single-file runner; carla_scenario.py forwards its old options to python -m bikeped.sim render.
  • Browser simulator restyled; it loads extra scenario suites from simulator/scenarios.extended.js when the file is present.
  • Copies of the calibration scripts and tools in the repository root removed. They live in calibration/ and tools/.

• Documentation and calibration updates.
  • Documentation fixes.

• Repository refactored; bridge_starter/ deployment kit added.
  • README and documentation updates.
• Code, testbench and scripts added.
• Initial commit.

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text:
Collisions between cyclists and pedestrians at urban intersections remain a persistent source of injuries, yet few systems attempt real-time warnings to unequipped road users using commodity hardware. We present a prototype collision warning system that runs on a single edge device with a wide-angle fisheye camera, producing audible and visual alerts at 30 fps. The system makes four contributions. First, we develop a calibration pipeline for ultra-wide fisheye lenses that overcomes corner-detection failure and optimizer divergence through perspective remapping and direct bundle adjustment. Second, we combine fisheye-aware object detection with a closed-form ground-plane projection via a precomputed lookup table. Third, we introduce a design-time conformance simulation with 24 scripted hazard scenarios, stochastic size-aware detection failures, and a latency sweep showing that a first-order kinematic predictor maintains the mean warning budget above the distracted-pedestrian reaction time across realistic camera latencies. Fourth, we formalize the decision layer as a separable, auditable testbench with explicit deployment gates, contestability mechanisms, and a residual risk register. Under conformance testing with fisheye localization error, the selected pipeline configuration achieves 93.3% sensitivity and 92.3% specificity, with a mean warning budget of 3.3 s. The system design was informed by community-aided design workshops. Code and replication scripts are available at https://github.com/mkturkcan/bikeped.

Where each contribution lives in this repository:

Contribution Code Documentation Fisheye calibration by perspective remapping and bundle adjustment calibration/ Calibration Ground-plane projection FisheyeCamera in decision_testbench.py Perception Conformance simulation, detection failures, latency sweep decision_testbench.py Testbench, uncertainty, latency Decision layer decision_pipeline.py Decision pipeline

The sensitivity and specificity in the abstract are the default row of python decision_testbench.py --compare. The quickstart shows that run.

docs.title: Dataset
docs.text: The 24 conformance scenarios are published on Hugging Face as mehmetkeremturkcan/bikeped, with per-frame ground-truth labels and three videos per scenario. This page describes what the dataset contains and how to read it.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
The dataset card names it "bikeped Conformance Scenarios". Agents follow hand-authored waypoint paths that are interpolated at 30 fps, and each frame carries a danger label from the kinematic safety model. The licence is CC BY 4.0.

Path Files Contents scenarios.jsonl 1 One row per scenario: metadata, waypoint paths and video paths. frames.jsonl 1 One row per scenario, agent and frame, with position and labels. videos/sim/ 24 Schematic simulated render of each scenario. videos/sim_2cam/ 24 A second schematic set. The folder name matches the _2cam suffix that sim_visualizer.py --two-cam gives its output. videos/carla/ 24 CARLA 0.9.16 renders from the pole camera on Town10HD_Opt.

Videos are named by index and slug, for example videos/carla/07_fast_approach.mp4. The dataset page reports a total file size of 389 MB.

docs.title: Configurations
docs.text: The two JSONL files are exposed as two configurations with a single train split each.

docs.title: scenarios
docs.text:
24 rows.

Column Type Meaning scenario_id int Index of the scenario, 0 to 23, in the order of decision_testbench.SCENARIOS. name string Display name, for example Fast Approach. expected_dominant string idle, safe, warning or alert. vehicle string Braking profile of the cyclist: bicycle or ebike. duration_s float Scenario length in seconds. n_person, n_bike int Number of pedestrians and cyclists. agents list One entry per agent with type, agent_id and path, a list of {x, y, t} waypoints. sim_video, carla_video string Paths of the schematic and the CARLA video inside the dataset.

docs.title: frames
docs.text:
12,901 rows.

Column Type Meaning scenario_id, scenario_name int, string Scenario the row belongs to. frame_idx, time_s int, float Frame index and time at 30 fps. agent_id, agent_type int, string Agent the position belongs to. x_m, y_m float Interpolated position in the scenario frame, in metres. is_danger bool Ground-truth danger label of the frame. actionable bool Whether a warning at this frame can still be acted on. severity float Severity, scaled by speed relative to 12 m/s. ttc_s float Time to collision in seconds. closing_speed_ms, bike_speed_ms float Closing speed of the pair and cyclist speed, in m/s. stopping_dist_m float Cyclist stopping distance in metres. warning_budget_s float Warning budget in seconds. distance_m float Distance to the nearest counterpart in metres.

docs.title: Coordinate frame
docs.text: Positions use the scenario frame of the testbench. The crosswalk runs along the y axis at x = 5 m and is about 3 m wide, cyclists travel along x, and the card places the deployed camera at (x = 5, y = -13, z = 3.66) in metres.

docs.title: Ground-truth labels
docs.text: The card describes the label as a conservative kinematic model: a frame is dangerous when the pair is closing, the closest approach is within 5 m, and either the stopping distance or the time to collision says the cyclist cannot avoid the conflict. Conventional bicycles use a reaction time of 0.84 s and a deceleration of 1.96 m/s², and e-bikes a deceleration of 6.0 m/s². 21 of the 24 scenarios contain a danger interval. The same model is implemented by compute_ground_truth_danger in decision_testbench.py, documented under safety model.

docs.title: Relation to the repository
docs.text: The waypoint paths in scenarios.jsonl are those of decision_testbench.SCENARIOS, so a result computed from the dataset can be checked against python decision_testbench.py. The repository also renders the videos: sim_visualizer.py writes the schematic ones and the CARLA renderer the photorealistic ones.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: Short answers to questions that come up when reading the paper, running the testbench or setting the system up at a new site. Each answer points to the page with the details.

docs.title: What do the four states mean?
docs.text: idle means no pedestrian is tracked. safe means a pedestrian is present and no cyclist has been seen within the cyclist memory. warning means a pedestrian is present and a cyclist is or recently was in the scene, but no pair passes the closing check. alert means a cyclist and a pedestrian are within the distance bounds, the distance between them is shrinking, and the cyclist is moving. The light shows blue, green, orange and red for the four states. See The decision pipeline.

docs.title: Why is there a warning state between safe and alert?
docs.text: Stage 3 returns alert only for a pair that is closing. When a cyclist is in the scene with a pedestrian and no pair meets that test, the pipeline falls through to warning and does not go back to safe. The light therefore shows that a cyclist is around before any conflict is detected.

docs.title: Why does the pipeline remember cyclists?
docs.text: Stage 2 keeps a memory of the times at which a cyclist was in the frame. It stays open for bike_memory_frames frames after the last one, 58 frames or about 1.9 s at 30 FPS with the shipped parameters. A cyclist that the detector drops for a few frames does not send the state back to safe. The testbench models such dropouts, see Detection and localisation uncertainty.

docs.title: Why pairwise closing and not time-to-collision or distance alone?
docs.text:
python decision_testbench.py --compare runs the default rule and three baseline rules on the 24 conformance scenarios. The baselines keep the default memory and lower bound. baseline_distance_only uses a 10 m upper bound and baseline_ttc a 3 s threshold. Totals over all frames, with fisheye localisation error enabled:

Rule Config name TP FP FN TN Sensitivity Specificity Pairwise closing default 1228 370 88 4418 93.3% 92.3% Distance only baseline_distance_only 761 1429 555 3359 57.8% 70.2% Naive closing baseline_naive_closing 1229 460 87 4328 93.4% 90.4% Time-to-collision baseline_ttc 1109 173 207 4615 84.3% 96.4%

The time-to-collision rule misses 207 danger frames where pairwise closing misses 88. Naive closing matches the sensitivity and raises 90 more false-positive frames. The decision pipeline defines each rule.

docs.title: Do I need a GPU?
docs.text: Not for the testbench, the figures or the paper tables. They need numpy, scipy, matplotlib, pyyaml and opencv-python. The live loop runs a YOLO detector at a 1280 px input size, and for that the README recommends a CUDA-capable GPU. The starter kit accepts YOLO_DEVICE = "cpu". The repository gives no throughput figure for that case.

docs.title: Can I use a different detector?
docs.text: Yes. In the starter kit, point YOLO_HF_REPO and YOLO_HF_FILE at other ultralytics weights. The kit assumes COCO class IDs: 0 is a pedestrian, and 1 and 3 are cyclists. With a detector outside ultralytics, replace the model.predict call. The decision pipeline itself only needs a track ID and a ground position in metres for each pedestrian and cyclist, passed to DecisionPipeline.update_track and evaluate.

docs.title: Why does a cyclist not trigger an alert against their own body?
docs.text: Detectors usually output a separate person box for the rider. The kit relabels a person box that overlaps a bicycle or motorcycle box as a cyclist, and the pipeline ignores pairs closer than prox_min, 1.9 m by default. Both thresholds depend on the camera geometry. See Tuning for a new site.

docs.title: Why is the fisheye not calibrated with OpenCV's fisheye module?
docs.text: OpenCV's fisheye calibration fits the Kannala-Brandt model with polynomial distortion coefficients. According to the docstring of calibrate_fisheye.py, that model does not fit the 200° spherical lens on a 16:9 sensor used here. The script fits the equidistant model r = f · θ directly with a bundle adjustment, with optional k1 and k2 correction terms. See Fisheye calibration.

docs.title: Where is the live MQTT bridge of the deployed system?
docs.text: mqtt_bridge.py is not in this repository. bridge_starter/ is a self-contained version of it with the same decision pipeline, a simulated light and optional sound, meant to be copied and adapted.

docs.title: Does editing config.yaml change the testbench results?
docs.text: Only camera.height and camera.pitch_deg are read by the testbench. The lens intrinsics come from camera_calibration.json, and the decision parameters come from PIPELINE_CONFIGS in decision_testbench.py. The other keys of config.yaml belong to the live bridge. See Configuration reference.

docs.title: Can I try the decision logic without a camera or any install?
docs.text: Yes. The browser simulator runs the pipeline on the conformance scenarios in a web page. For numbers, run the testbench, which needs Python and the packages in requirements.txt.

docs.title: How do I cite the project?
docs.text: See Citing for the BibTeX entry of the paper, arXiv 2604.17046.

Command line interface: python -m bikeped.scenarios COMMAND.

Run from the repository root so that decision_testbench is importable.

docs.title: build_parser
docs.text:
build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser

Argument parser for all subcommands.

Source code in bikeped/scenarios/cli.py 
def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    """Argument parser for all subcommands."""
    from .generators import FAMILIES

    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog='python -m bikeped.scenarios',
        description='List, check, evaluate, generate and export bike-pedestrian scenarios. '
                    'Suites: ' + ', '.join(list_suites()) + '.')
    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest='command', required=True, metavar='COMMAND')

    sp = sub.add_parser('list', help='list scenarios with suite, family, agents and duration')
    sp.add_argument('--suite', help='only this suite')
    sp.add_argument('--family', help='only this family')
    sp.add_argument('--json', action='store_true', help='print metadata as JSON')
    sp.set_defaults(func=_cmd_list)

    sp = sub.add_parser('show', help='print one scenario as JSON')
    sp.add_argument('id', metavar='ID',
                    help="slug, exact name, or suite:index with a zero-based index "
                         "(e.g. conformance:7)")
    sp.set_defaults(func=_cmd_show)

    sp = sub.add_parser('validate', help='check format, speeds and unique ids; exit 1 on problems')
    sp.add_argument('--suite', help='only this suite (ids are checked for uniqueness within it)')
    sp.set_defaults(func=_cmd_validate)

    sp = sub.add_parser(
        'evaluate', help='run the decision pipeline with ideal perception and summarise',
        description='Simulate each scenario with decision_testbench.simulate_scenario and print '
                    'ground-truth danger time, alert time, false-alert time, the lead of the '
                    'alert over each danger interval (negative means late) and the dominant '
                    'state against the expected one.')
    sp.add_argument('--suite', help='only this suite (default: all registered suites)')
    sp.add_argument('--config', default='default',
                    help='key of decision_testbench.PIPELINE_CONFIGS (default: default)')
    sp.add_argument('--json', action='store_true', help='print rows as JSON')
    sp.set_defaults(func=_cmd_evaluate)

    sp = sub.add_parser('generate', help='write a seeded parametric suite as JSON',
                        description='Families: ' + '; '.join(f'{k}: {v}'
                                                             for k, v in FAMILIES.items()))
    sp.add_argument('--family', required=True, choices=list(FAMILIES))
    sp.add_argument('--n', type=int, default=20, help='number of scenarios (default 20)')
    sp.add_argument('--seed', type=int, default=0, help='random seed (default 0)')
    sp.add_argument('--out', default='-', help='output JSON file, - for stdout (default)')
    sp.set_defaults(func=_cmd_generate)

    sp = sub.add_parser('export', help='write catalog.json and one SVG thumbnail per scenario')
    sp.add_argument('--out', required=True, help='output directory')
    sp.add_argument('--simulator', metavar='DIR',
                    help='also write DIR/scenarios.extended.js for the browser simulator')
    sp.set_defaults(func=_cmd_export)
    return p

def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Parse ``argv`` and run the chosen command; returns the exit status."""
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    return int(args.func(args))

docs.title: builders
docs.text:
Path builders that emit the testbench waypoint format.

Every builder works in the scenario frame used by decision_testbench: metres, x along the road (bikes ride along it), y across the road (pedestrians cross along it), crosswalk centre at (5, 0). Times are seconds from the start of the scenario and speeds are metres per second.

The testbench interpolates paths linearly in time, so curved or speed-varying motion is sampled densely (every step seconds, 0.25 s by default). Headings are in degrees, counter-clockwise from +x: 0 rides towards +x, 180 towards -x (the direction of the conformance bikes), 90 walks towards +y.

The fluent :class:Path keeps scenario definitions short::

bike = (Path.start(34, 1.5, heading=180).ride(14, 6.0)
        .arc(radius=6, angle=90).ride(8).build())

docs.title: Path
docs.text:
Path(
    x: float,
    y: float,
    t: float = 0.0,
    heading: float = 0.0,
    speed: float = 0.0,
    step: float = 0.25,
)

Fluent builder for one agent path.

The builder tracks the current position (x, y) in metres, time t in seconds, heading in degrees and speed in m/s. Each motion primitive appends waypoints sampled every step seconds and leaves the state at its end, so primitives chain. :meth:build returns the waypoint list with strictly increasing times.

Source code in bikeped/scenarios/builders.py 
def __init__(self, x: float, y: float, t: float = 0.0, heading: float = 0.0,
             speed: float = 0.0, step: float = 0.25) -> None:
    self.x, self.y, self.t = float(x), float(y), float(t)
    self.heading = float(heading)
    self.speed = float(speed)
    self.step = float(step)
    self._points: list[tuple[float, float, float]] = [(self.x, self.y, self.t)]

docs.title: ride
docs.text:
ride(distance: float, speed: float | None = None) -> Path

Move distance metres along the current heading at constant speed (m/s).

Source code in bikeped/scenarios/builders.py 
def ride(self, distance: float, speed: float | None = None) -> Path:
    """Move ``distance`` metres along the current heading at constant ``speed`` (m/s)."""
    if speed is not None:
        self.speed = float(speed)
    if self.speed <= 0:
        raise ValueError('ride() needs a positive speed')
    ux, uy = self._unit()
    x0, y0, t0 = self.x, self.y, self.t
    dur = distance / self.speed
    n = max(1, math.ceil(dur / self.step))
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        f = i / n
        self._emit(x0 + ux * distance * f, y0 + uy * distance * f, t0 + dur * f)
    return self

docs.title: to
docs.text:
to(x: float, y: float, speed: float | None = None) -> Path

Move in a straight line to (x, y) at constant speed; the heading follows.

Source code in bikeped/scenarios/builders.py 
def to(self, x: float, y: float, speed: float | None = None) -> Path:
    """Move in a straight line to ``(x, y)`` at constant ``speed``; the heading follows."""
    dx, dy = x - self.x, y - self.y
    dist = math.hypot(dx, dy)
    if dist < 1e-9:
        return self
    self.heading = math.degrees(math.atan2(dy, dx))
    return self.ride(dist, speed)

def wait(self, duration: float) -> Path:
    """Stand still for ``duration`` seconds; the speed becomes zero."""
    self.speed = 0.0
    self._emit(self.x, self.y, self.t + duration)
    return self

docs.title: appear
docs.text:
appear(t: float) -> Path

Shift the whole path so that it begins at time t.

Use it for late emergence: the agent is absent (not detected) until t, as if hidden behind a parked van or a crowd. Call it before any motion primitive.

Source code in bikeped/scenarios/builders.py 
def appear(self, t: float) -> Path:
    """Shift the whole path so that it begins at time ``t``.

    Use it for late emergence: the agent is absent (not detected) until ``t``, as if hidden
    behind a parked van or a crowd. Call it before any motion primitive.
    """
    if len(self._points) != 1:
        raise ValueError('appear() must be called before the first motion')
    self.t = float(t)
    self._points = [(self.x, self.y, self.t)]
    return self

docs.title: change_speed
docs.text:
change_speed(v_end: float, accel: float) -> Path

Accelerate or brake along the heading to v_end m/s at |accel| m/s^2.

The distance covered follows from constant acceleration; the path ends with speed == v_end. Braking to zero leaves the agent stopped at the end point.

Source code in bikeped/scenarios/builders.py 
def change_speed(self, v_end: float, accel: float) -> Path:
    """Accelerate or brake along the heading to ``v_end`` m/s at ``|accel|`` m/s^2.

    The distance covered follows from constant acceleration; the path ends with
    ``speed == v_end``. Braking to zero leaves the agent stopped at the end point.
    """
    a = abs(float(accel))
    v0 = self.speed
    if a <= 0 or abs(v_end - v0) < 1e-9:
        return self
    sign = 1.0 if v_end > v0 else -1.0
    dur = abs(v_end - v0) / a
    ux, uy = self._unit()
    x0, y0, t0 = self.x, self.y, self.t
    n = max(1, math.ceil(dur / self.step))
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        tt = dur * i / n
        s = v0 * tt + 0.5 * sign * a * tt * tt
        self._emit(x0 + ux * s, y0 + uy * s, t0 + tt)
    self.speed = float(v_end)
    return self

docs.title: brake_to
docs.text:
brake_to(x: float | None = None, y: float | None = None, v_end: float = 0.0) -> Path

Brake at constant deceleration so the agent reaches v_end at a given coordinate.

Give x (for agents moving along the road) or y (for agents moving across it). The deceleration is whatever stops the agent exactly there.

Source code in bikeped/scenarios/builders.py 
def brake_to(self, x: float | None = None, y: float | None = None,
             v_end: float = 0.0) -> Path:
    """Brake at constant deceleration so the agent reaches ``v_end`` at a given coordinate.

    Give ``x`` (for agents moving along the road) or ``y`` (for agents moving across it). The
    deceleration is whatever stops the agent exactly there.
    """
    ux, uy = self._unit()
    if x is not None:
        dist = (x - self.x) / ux if abs(ux) > 1e-6 else math.nan
    elif y is not None:
        dist = (y - self.y) / uy if abs(uy) > 1e-6 else math.nan
    else:
        raise ValueError('brake_to() needs x or y')
    if not dist > 0:
        raise ValueError('brake_to() target lies behind the agent')
    decel = (self.speed ** 2 - v_end ** 2) / (2.0 * dist)
    if decel <= 0:
        raise ValueError('brake_to() needs v_end below the current speed')
    return self.change_speed(v_end, decel)

docs.title: arc
docs.text:
arc(radius: float, angle: float, speed: float | None = None) -> Path

Turn on a circular arc of radius metres through angle degrees.

Positive angles turn left (counter-clockwise seen from above, +y up), negative angles turn right. Speed is constant along the arc.

Source code in bikeped/scenarios/builders.py 
def arc(self, radius: float, angle: float, speed: float | None = None) -> Path:
    """Turn on a circular arc of ``radius`` metres through ``angle`` degrees.

    Positive angles turn left (counter-clockwise seen from above, ``+y`` up), negative angles
    turn right. Speed is constant along the arc.
    """
    if speed is not None:
        self.speed = float(speed)
    if self.speed <= 0:
        raise ValueError('arc() needs a positive speed')
    sgn = 1.0 if angle >= 0 else -1.0
    h0 = math.radians(self.heading)
    cx = self.x - sgn * radius * math.sin(h0)
    cy = self.y + sgn * radius * math.cos(h0)
    length = radius * math.radians(abs(angle))
    dur = length / self.speed
    n = max(2, math.ceil(dur / self.step))
    t0 = self.t
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        phi = h0 + sgn * math.radians(abs(angle)) * i / n
        self._emit(cx + sgn * radius * math.sin(phi), cy - sgn * radius * math.cos(phi),
                   t0 + dur * i / n)
    self.heading += angle
    return self

docs.title: lane_change
docs.text:
lane_change(lateral: float, length: float, speed: float | None = None) -> Path

Shift sideways by lateral metres (positive to the left) over length metres.

The lateral offset follows a half-cosine, which gives a smooth swerve or lane change; the heading is unchanged at the end.

Source code in bikeped/scenarios/builders.py 
def lane_change(self, lateral: float, length: float, speed: float | None = None) -> Path:
    """Shift sideways by ``lateral`` metres (positive to the left) over ``length`` metres.

    The lateral offset follows a half-cosine, which gives a smooth swerve or lane change; the
    heading is unchanged at the end.
    """
    if speed is not None:
        self.speed = float(speed)
    ux, uy = self._unit()
    lx, ly = -uy, ux
    x0, y0, t0 = self.x, self.y, self.t
    dur = math.hypot(length, lateral) / self.speed
    n = max(4, math.ceil(dur / self.step))
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        f = i / n
        off = lateral * 0.5 * (1.0 - math.cos(math.pi * f))
        self._emit(x0 + ux * length * f + lx * off, y0 + uy * length * f + ly * off,
                   t0 + dur * f)
    return self

docs.text:
zigzag(
    distance: float, amplitude: float, wavelength: float, speed: float | None = None
) -> Path

Weave about the current heading: sinusoidal lateral offset of amplitude metres.

The agent covers distance metres along the heading; one full weave takes wavelength metres. Speed is the speed along the heading.

Source code in bikeped/scenarios/builders.py 
def zigzag(self, distance: float, amplitude: float, wavelength: float,
           speed: float | None = None) -> Path:
    """Weave about the current heading: sinusoidal lateral offset of ``amplitude`` metres.

    The agent covers ``distance`` metres along the heading; one full weave takes
    ``wavelength`` metres. Speed is the speed along the heading.
    """
    if speed is not None:
        self.speed = float(speed)
    ux, uy = self._unit()
    lx, ly = -uy, ux
    x0, y0, t0 = self.x, self.y, self.t
    dur = distance / self.speed
    n = max(4, math.ceil(dur / self.step))
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        s = distance * i / n
        off = amplitude * math.sin(2.0 * math.pi * s / wavelength)
        self._emit(x0 + ux * s + lx * off, y0 + uy * s + ly * off, t0 + dur * i / n)
    return self

docs.title: through
docs.text:
through(points: Sequence[tuple[float, float]], speed: float | None = None) -> Path

Follow a Catmull-Rom spline from the current position through points at speed.

The spline passes through every control point. Arc length is resampled so the speed is constant; the heading at the end follows the last segment.

Source code in bikeped/scenarios/builders.py 
def through(self, points: Sequence[tuple[float, float]], speed: float | None = None) -> Path:
    """Follow a Catmull-Rom spline from the current position through ``points`` at ``speed``.

    The spline passes through every control point. Arc length is resampled so the speed is
    constant; the heading at the end follows the last segment.
    """
    if speed is not None:
        self.speed = float(speed)
    xy = catmull_rom([(self.x, self.y), *points], samples_per_segment=24)
    seg = np.hypot(np.diff(xy[:, 0]), np.diff(xy[:, 1]))
    s = np.concatenate([[0.0], np.cumsum(seg)])
    total = float(s[-1])
    dur = total / self.speed
    n = max(2, math.ceil(dur / self.step))
    t0 = self.t
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        si = total * i / n
        self._emit(float(np.interp(si, s, xy[:, 0])), float(np.interp(si, s, xy[:, 1])),
                   t0 + dur * i / n)
    dx, dy = xy[-1] - xy[-2]
    self.heading = math.degrees(math.atan2(dy, dx))
    return self

def build(self) -> list[Waypoint]:
    """Return the path as testbench waypoints ``[{'x', 'y', 't'}, ...]`` (rounded to mm, ms)."""
    out: list[Waypoint] = []
    for x, y, t in self._points:
        p = {'x': _round(x), 'y': _round(y), 't': _round(t)}
        if out and p['t'] <= out[-1]['t']:
            continue
        out.append(p)
    if len(out) < 2:

docs.title: catmull_rom
docs.text:
catmull_rom(
    points: Sequence[tuple[float, float]], samples_per_segment: int = 16
) -> np.ndarray

Sample a centripetal-free (uniform) Catmull-Rom spline through points.

Returns an (N, 2) array in the same units as the input. End points are duplicated so the curve starts and ends exactly at the first and last control points.

Source code in bikeped/scenarios/builders.py 
def catmull_rom(points: Sequence[tuple[float, float]], samples_per_segment: int = 16) -> np.ndarray:
    """Sample a centripetal-free (uniform) Catmull-Rom spline through ``points``.

    Returns an ``(N, 2)`` array in the same units as the input. End points are duplicated so the
    curve starts and ends exactly at the first and last control points.
    """
    p = np.asarray(points, dtype=float)
    if len(p) < 2:
        raise ValueError('catmull_rom() needs at least two points')
    ext = np.vstack([p[0], p, p[-1]])
    out = [p[0]]
    for i in range(1, len(ext) - 2):
        p0, p1, p2, p3 = ext[i - 1], ext[i], ext[i + 1], ext[i + 2]
        for k in range(1, samples_per_segment + 1):
            u = k / samples_per_segment
            u2, u3 = u * u, u * u * u
            out.append(0.5 * ((2 * p1) + (-p0 + p2) * u + (2 * p0 - 5 * p1 + 4 * p2 - p3) * u2
                              + (-p0 + 3 * p1 - 3 * p2 + p3) * u3))
    return np.asarray(out)

docs.text:
platoon(
    path: Sequence[Waypoint],
    n: int,
    headway_s: float = 1.0,
    lateral: float = 0.0,
    jitter_m: float = 0.0,
    jitter_s: float = 0.0,
    seed: int = 0,
    lateral_axis: str = "y",
) -> list[list[Waypoint]]

n riders on the same line, each headway_s seconds behind the previous one.

lateral staggers alternate riders sideways (metres along lateral_axis); jitter_m and jitter_s add seeded uniform noise to each rider's lateral position and start time so the group does not look cloned. The result is deterministic for a given seed.

Source code in bikeped/scenarios/builders.py 
def platoon(path: Sequence[Waypoint], n: int, headway_s: float = 1.0, lateral: float = 0.0,
            jitter_m: float = 0.0, jitter_s: float = 0.0, seed: int = 0,
            lateral_axis: str = 'y') -> list[list[Waypoint]]:
    """``n`` riders on the same line, each ``headway_s`` seconds behind the previous one.

    ``lateral`` staggers alternate riders sideways (metres along ``lateral_axis``); ``jitter_m``
    and ``jitter_s`` add seeded uniform noise to each rider's lateral position and start time so
    the group does not look cloned. The result is deterministic for a given ``seed``.
    """
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    out = []
    for i in range(n):
        side = lateral * (1 if i % 2 else 0)
        off = side + (rng.uniform(-jitter_m, jitter_m) if jitter_m else 0.0)
        dt = i * headway_s + (rng.uniform(0, jitter_s) if jitter_s and i else 0.0)
        if lateral_axis == 'y':
            out.append(shift(path, dy=off, dt=dt))
        else:
            out.append(shift(path, dx=off, dt=dt))
    return out

def path_speeds(path: Sequence[Waypoint]) -> np.ndarray:
    """Segment speeds (m/s) of a waypoint path, one per segment."""
    xs = np.array([p['x'] for p in path], dtype=float)
    ys = np.array([p['y'] for p in path], dtype=float)

docs.text:
path_accelerations(path: Sequence[Waypoint]) -> np.ndarray

Magnitude of the velocity change (m/s^2) at each interior waypoint.

The velocity change between consecutive segments is divided by the time between segment midpoints, so turns contribute their centripetal acceleration.

Source code in bikeped/scenarios/builders.py 
def path_accelerations(path: Sequence[Waypoint]) -> np.ndarray:
    """Magnitude of the velocity change (m/s^2) at each interior waypoint.

    The velocity change between consecutive segments is divided by the time between segment
    midpoints, so turns contribute their centripetal acceleration.
    """
    xs = np.array([p['x'] for p in path], dtype=float)
    ys = np.array([p['y'] for p in path], dtype=float)
    ts = np.array([p['t'] for p in path], dtype=float)
    if len(ts) < 3:
        return np.zeros(0)
    dts = np.diff(ts)
    vx, vy = np.diff(xs) / dts, np.diff(ys) / dts
    mid = 0.5 * (dts[:-1] + dts[1:])
    return np.hypot(np.diff(vx), np.diff(vy)) / mid

The view is the window x in [-12, 36], y in [-15, 15] (metres), widened at the same aspect ratio when a scenario's paths leave it, so most thumbnails share one scale. def thumbnail_svg(s: dict) -> str:
    """SVG source of the thumbnail for scenario ``s`` (320x200 viewBox, no text)."""
    x0, x1, y0, y1 = _window(s)
    k = W / (x1 - x0)

    def px(x: float) -> float:
        return (x - x0) * k

    def py(y: float) -> float:
        return (y1 - y) * k

    out = ['<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 320 200" width="320" '
           'height="200">',
           f'<rect width="320" height="200" fill="{BG}"/>',
           f'<rect x="0" y="{_f(py(ROAD_HALF))}" width="320" '
           f'height="{_f(2 * ROAD_HALF * k)}" fill="{ROAD}"/>']
    for yk in (ROAD_HALF, -ROAD_HALF):
        out.append(f'<line x1="0" y1="{_f(py(yk))}" x2="320" y2="{_f(py(yk))}" '
                   f'stroke="{KERB}" stroke-width="1.5"/>')
    out.append(f'<line x1="0" y1="{_f(py(0))}" x2="320" y2="{_f(py(0))}" stroke="{LANE}" '
               f'stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="8 8"/>')
    sx0, sx1 = px(CROSSWALK_X[0]), px(CROSSWALK_X[1])
    y = -ROAD_HALF + 0.3
    while y + 0.6 <= ROAD_HALF:
        out.append(f'<rect x="{_f(sx0)}" y="{_f(py(y + 0.6))}" width="{_f(sx1 - sx0)}" '
                   f'height="{_f(0.6 * k)}" fill="{STRIPE}"/>')
        y += 1.2
    # Pedestrians are drawn last so that they stay visible where a bike path crosses them.
    for agent in sorted(s['agents'], key=lambda a: a['type'] == 'person'):
        out.extend(_agent_svg(agent, px, py))
    out.append('</svg>')
    return '\n'.join(out) + '\n'

def export_catalog(out_dir: str | FsPath, suites: Iterable[str] | None = None) -> dict:
    """Write ``catalog.json`` and ``<id>.svg`` for every scenario of ``suites`` into ``out_dir``.

    Returns ``{'catalog': path, 'thumbnails': n, 'scenarios': n}``.
    """
    out = FsPath(out_dir)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    names = list(suites) if suites is not None else list_suites()
    records = []
    for name in names:
        for s in get_suite(name):
            (out / f"{s['id']}.svg").write_text(thumbnail_svg(s), encoding='utf-8')
            records.append(scenario_record(s))
    catalog = {
        'frame': 'metres; x along the road, y across it; crosswalk centre at (5, 0)',
        'suites': {n: [r['id'] for r in records if r['suite'] == n] for n in names},
        'families': _family_names(),
        'scenarios': records,
    }
    path = out / 'catalog.json'
    path.write_text(json.dumps(catalog, indent=1) + '\n', encoding='utf-8')
    return {'catalog': str(path), 'thumbnails': len(records), 'scenarios': len(records)}

def export_simulator(sim_dir: str | FsPath, suites: Iterable[str] = ('extended', 'stress')
                     ) -> str:
    """Write ``scenarios.extended.js`` for the browser simulator in ``sim_dir``.

    The file defines ``window.BIKEPED_SUITES = {suite: [scenario, ...]}`` with the simulator's
    own scenario keys (``name``, ``expected``, ``challenge``, ``agents``) plus ``id``, ``family``
    and ``vehicle``, so the page loads it with a plain ``<script src>`` even from ``file://``.
    """
    data = {}
    for name in suites:
        data[name] = [{
            'id': s['id'], 'name': s['name'], 'expected': s['expected_dominant'],
            'family': s.get('family', ''), 'challenge': s.get('description', ''),
            'vehicle': s.get('vehicle', 'bicycle'),
            'agents': [{'type': a['type'], 'id': a['id'], 'path': a['path']}
                       for a in s['agents']],
        } for s in get_suite(name)]
    path = FsPath(sim_dir) / 'scenarios.extended.js'
    path.write_text('// Extended scenario suites for index.html, written by '
                    '"python -m bikeped.scenarios export --simulator".\n'
                    'window.BIKEPED_SUITES = ' + json.dumps(data, separators=(',', ':')) + ';\n',
                    encoding='utf-8')
    return str(path)

def conformance_suite() -> list[dict]:
    """The paper's 24 scenarios in paper order, as decorated shallow copies.

    Each copy shares the waypoint lists with ``decision_testbench.SCENARIOS``; the agent dicts are
    copied so that the ``model`` hints do not touch the originals.
    """
    import decision_testbench as tb

    out = []
    for original in tb.SCENARIOS:
        family, description, tags, models = META[original['name']]
        s = dict(original)
        s['agents'] = []
        for agent in original['agents']:
            a = dict(agent)
            if agent['id'] in models:
                a['model'] = models[agent['id']]
            s['agents'].append(a)
        s.update(id=slugify(original['name']), suite='conformance', family=family,
                 description=description, tags=list(tags))
        out.append(s)
    return out

docs.title: evaluate
docs.text:
Run scenarios through the testbench decision pipeline and summarise the outcome.

Everything is computed by decision_testbench.simulate_scenario with ideal perception (the noise-free path, tracker on, no latency). This module only aggregates its per-frame states and ground-truth dangers into per-scenario figures; the metrics themselves (danger labels, false positives, sensitivity) are the testbench's.

The dominant state of a run is the most severe state (alert > warning > safe > idle) that the pipeline holds for at least :data:MIN_STATE_S seconds in total. The same rule applied to the ground truth gives :func:ground_truth_label: idle without pedestrians, safe without cyclists, alert with at least :data:MIN_STATE_S of danger, else warning.

def dominant_state(states: Sequence[str], fps: int = FPS, min_s: float = MIN_STATE_S) -> str:
    """Most severe state held for at least ``min_s`` seconds in total (``idle`` if none)."""
    states = np.asarray(states)
    for state in reversed(SEVERITY):
        if np.sum(states == state) / fps >= min_s:
            return state
    return 'idle'

def ground_truth_label(scenario: dict, dangers: np.ndarray, fps: int = FPS,
                       min_s: float = MIN_STATE_S) -> str:
    """State the ground truth calls for: see the module docstring for the rule."""
    types = {a['type'] for a in scenario['agents']}
    if 'person' not in types:
        return 'idle'
    if 'bike' not in types:
        return 'safe'
    return 'alert' if np.sum(dangers) / fps >= min_s else 'warning'

def label_scenario(scenario: dict, fps: int = FPS) -> str:
    """:func:`ground_truth_label` from ``compute_ground_truth_danger`` alone (no pipeline run).

    The frame times match ``simulate_scenario``: ``t = k / fps`` up to the scenario duration.
    """
    tb = _tb()
    duration = tb.get_scenario_duration(scenario)
    n = int(math.floor(duration * fps + 1e-9)) + 1
    dangers = np.array([tb.compute_ground_truth_danger(scenario, k / fps).is_danger
                        for k in range(n)], dtype=bool)
    return ground_truth_label(scenario, dangers, fps)

evaluate_scenario(scenario: dict, config: str = 'default', fps: int = FPS) -> dict

Simulate one scenario and summarise it.

Returned keys: id, name, suite, family, duration_s, agents, danger_s and actionable_s (ground-truth time), alert_s, false_alert_s (alert on frames the ground truth calls safe), danger_intervals (one dict per interval with start, end, alerted and lead_s: seconds from alert onset to danger onset, negative when the alert came late), sensitivity, specificity, dominant, expected, ground_truth and match.

Source code in bikeped/scenarios/evaluate.py 
def evaluate_scenario(scenario: dict, config: str = 'default', fps: int = FPS) -> dict:
    """Simulate one scenario and summarise it.

    Returned keys: ``id``, ``name``, ``suite``, ``family``, ``duration_s``, ``agents``,
    ``danger_s`` and ``actionable_s`` (ground-truth time), ``alert_s``, ``false_alert_s`` (alert
    on frames the ground truth calls safe), ``danger_intervals`` (one dict per interval with
    ``start``, ``end``, ``alerted`` and ``lead_s``: seconds from alert onset to danger onset,
    negative when the alert came late), ``sensitivity``, ``specificity``, ``dominant``,
    ``expected``, ``ground_truth`` and ``match``.
    """
    tb = _tb()
    params = tb.PIPELINE_CONFIGS[config]
    r = tb.simulate_scenario(scenario, params, fps=fps)
    times, states, dangers = r['times'], r['states'], r['dangers']
    dt = 1.0 / fps
    is_alert = states == 'alert'
    actionable = np.array([a.actionable for a in r['assessments']], dtype=bool)
    intervals = []
    for i0, i1 in _runs(dangers):
        lo = max(0, i0 - int(round(LEAD_WINDOW_S * fps)))
        hits = np.flatnonzero(is_alert[lo:i1])
        if len(hits):
            first = lo + int(hits[0])
            while first > 0 and is_alert[first - 1]:
                first -= 1
            lead = float(times[i0] - times[first])
            intervals.append({'start': round(float(times[i0]), 3),
                              'end': round(float(times[i1 - 1]) + dt, 3),
                              'alerted': True, 'lead_s': round(lead, 3)})
        else:
            intervals.append({'start': round(float(times[i0]), 3),
                              'end': round(float(times[i1 - 1]) + dt, 3),
                              'alerted': False, 'lead_s': None})
    dominant = dominant_state(states, fps)
    expected = scenario.get('expected_dominant')
    return {
        'id': scenario.get('id', ''),
        'name': scenario['name'],
        'suite': scenario.get('suite', ''),
        'family': scenario.get('family', ''),
        'duration_s': round(float(tb.get_scenario_duration(scenario)), 3),
        'agents': len(scenario['agents']),
        'danger_s': round(float(np.sum(dangers)) * dt, 3),
        'actionable_s': round(float(np.sum(actionable)) * dt, 3),
        'alert_s': round(float(np.sum(is_alert)) * dt, 3),
        'false_alert_s': round(r['false_pos'] * dt, 3),
        'danger_intervals': intervals,
        'sensitivity': round(float(r['sensitivity']), 4),
        'specificity': round(float(r['specificity']), 4),
        'dominant': dominant,
        'expected': expected,
        'ground_truth': ground_truth_label(scenario, dangers, fps),
        'match': dominant == expected,
        'tags': list(scenario.get('tags', [])),
    }

Source code in bikeped/scenarios/evaluate.py 
def is_known_hard(row: dict) -> bool:
    """True when the pipeline's dominant state is wrong or an alert is late or missing.

    Late means the alert began more than :data:`LATE_ALERT_S` seconds after the danger interval.
    """
    if not row['match']:
        return True
    return any(not d['alerted'] or d['lead_s'] < -LATE_ALERT_S for d in row['danger_intervals'])

def format_table(rows: Sequence[dict]) -> str:
    """Plain-text table of :func:`evaluate_scenario` rows with a totals line."""
    head = (f"{'scenario':<34} {'dur':>5} {'ag':>3} {'danger':>6} {'alert':>6} {'false':>6} "
            f"{'lead s (per interval)':<22} {'dominant':>8} {'expected':>8}  ok")
    lines = [head, '-' * len(head)]
    for r in rows:
        lines.append(
            f"{r['id'][:34]:<34} {r['duration_s']:>5.1f} {r['agents']:>3} {r['danger_s']:>6.2f} "
            f"{r['alert_s']:>6.2f} {r['false_alert_s']:>6.2f} "
            f"{_fmt_lead(r['danger_intervals'])[:22]:<22} {r['dominant']:>8} "
            f"{str(r['expected']):>8}  {'yes' if r['match'] else 'NO'}")
    n_iv = sum(len(r['danger_intervals']) for r in rows)
    n_ok = sum(1 for r in rows for d in r['danger_intervals']
               if d['alerted'] and d['lead_s'] >= -1.0 / FPS - 1e-9)
    lines.append('-' * len(head))
    lines.append(f"{len(rows)} scenarios, dominant state matches expected in "
                 f"{sum(r['match'] for r in rows)}; {n_ok} of {n_iv} danger intervals alerted "
                 f"no later than one frame after onset; false-alert time "
                 f"{sum(r['false_alert_s'] for r in rows):.2f} s")
    return '\n'.join(lines)

def to_json(rows: Sequence[dict]) -> str:
    """JSON text of evaluation rows (non-finite numbers become ``null``)."""
    def clean(v):
        if isinstance(v, float) and not math.isfinite(v):
            return None
        if isinstance(v, dict):
            return {k: clean(x) for k, x in v.items()}
        if isinstance(v, list):
            return [clean(x) for x in v]
        return v

    return json.dumps([clean(r) for r in rows], indent=2)

docs.title: extended
docs.text:
The extended suite: hand-designed urban conflicts and deliberate negatives.

Same frame as the conformance scenarios: metres, x along the road, y across it, the crosswalk centred on (5, 0) and about 3 m wide, kerbs near y = -6.5 and y = +6.5. Through cyclists ride towards -x (heading 180 degrees) a metre or two either side of the centre line, as in the paper's scenarios.

Speeds follow published ranges: walking 1.2-1.5 m/s, older adults 0.8-1.0, wheelchairs 1.0-1.3, children running 2-3, runners 3-4, commuter cyclists 4-7, fast road cyclists 8-11, e-bikes up to about 11, e-scooters 5-7, cargo bikes 3.5-5.5; comfortable cyclist braking about 2 m/s^2 and hard braking 4-6 m/s^2.

expected_dominant is the label the testbench ground truth implies (:func:bikeped.scenarios.evaluate.ground_truth_label), checked by running each scenario. Scenarios the default pipeline gets wrong carry the known-hard tag: its dominant state differs from expected_dominant (a false alarm or a miss), or its first alert comes more than :data:~bikeped.scenarios.evaluate.LATE_ALERT_S after a danger interval begins.

def along(speed: float, t_at: float, y: float = 1.0, x_at: float = 5.0, x_end: float = -8.0,
          max_start: float = 34.0) -> list[dict]:
    """Cyclist riding towards ``-x`` at ``speed`` that reaches ``x_at`` at time ``t_at``.

    It starts at ``t = 0`` far enough back to arrive on time, or later if that would put it more
    than ``max_start`` metres down the road.
    """
    x0 = x_at + speed * t_at
    t0 = 0.0
    if x0 > max_start:
        t0 = t_at - (max_start - x_at) / speed
        x0 = max_start
    return Path.start(x0, y, t0).to(x_end, y, speed).build()

docs.title: generators
docs.text:
Seeded parametric scenario families.

generate(family, n, seed) returns n scenarios of one family in the usual frame (metres, x along the road, crosswalk centred on (5, 0)). Sweep families spread their parameter evenly over the range in :data:FAMILIES and use the seed only for small jitter (start times within 0.2 s, speeds within 5 %), so the sweep values themselves stay readable. The same family, n and seed always give identical output.

expected_dominant of each generated scenario is computed from the testbench ground truth with :func:bikeped.scenarios.evaluate.label_scenario.

docs.title: generate
docs.text:
generate(family: str, n: int = 20, seed: int = 0) -> list[dict]

n scenarios of family (a key of :data:FAMILIES), deterministic for seed.

Source code in bikeped/scenarios/generators.py 
def generate(family: str, n: int = 20, seed: int = 0) -> list[dict]:
    """``n`` scenarios of ``family`` (a key of :data:`FAMILIES`), deterministic for ``seed``."""
    if family not in FAMILIES:
        raise KeyError(f'unknown family {family!r}; known: {", ".join(FAMILIES)}')
    if n < 1:
        raise ValueError('n must be at least 1')
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)

    def jt() -> float:
        return float(rng.uniform(-0.2, 0.2))

    def js(v: float) -> float:
        return v * float(rng.uniform(0.95, 1.05))

    out: list[dict] = []
    if family == 'crossing-angle':
        for ang in _sweep(30.0, 150.0, n):
            out.append(_base(
                f'Crossing at {ang:.0f} deg',
                f'A pedestrian crosses at {ang:.0f} degrees to the road and reaches the lane '
                f'centre as a {BIKE_SPEED:.0f} m/s cyclist arrives.',
                [ped(1, _cross_through((5.0, 0.0), ang, js(PED_SPEED), T_CONFLICT + jt())),
                 bike(2, _ride(js(BIKE_SPEED), T_CONFLICT + jt()))]))
    elif family == 'cyclist-speed':
        for v in _sweep(3.0, 11.0, n):
            out.append(_base(
                f'Cyclist at {v:.1f} m/s',
                f'A cyclist at {v:.1f} m/s reaches the crosswalk as the pedestrian is mid-lane.',
                [ped(1, _cross_through((5.0, 0.0), 90.0, js(PED_SPEED), T_CONFLICT + jt())),
                 bike(2, _ride(js(v), T_CONFLICT + jt()),
                      model='ebike' if v > 8.5 else 'bicycle')],
                vehicle='ebike' if v > 8.5 else 'bicycle'))
    elif family == 'time-gap':
        for gap in _sweep(-3.0, 3.0, n):
            out.append(_base(
                f'Time gap {gap:+.1f} s',
                f'The cyclist reaches the conflict point {abs(gap):.1f} s '
                f'{"after" if gap >= 0 else "before"} the pedestrian.',
                [ped(1, _cross_through((5.0, 0.0), 90.0, js(PED_SPEED), T_CONFLICT)),
                 bike(2, _ride(js(BIKE_SPEED), T_CONFLICT + gap + 0.5 * jt()))]))
    elif family == 'lateral-offset':
        for off in _sweep(0.0, 5.0, n):
            out.append(_base(
                f'Lateral offset {off:.1f} m',
                f'The cyclist passes {off:.1f} m to the side of the pedestrian at the moment '
                f'of crossing.',
                [ped(1, _cross_through((5.0, 0.0), 90.0, js(PED_SPEED), T_CONFLICT + jt())),
                 bike(2, _ride(js(BIKE_SPEED), T_CONFLICT, y=off))]))
    elif family == 'group-size':
        for k in range(1, n + 1):
            lead = _cross_through((5.0, 0.0), 90.0, PED_SPEED, T_CONFLICT)
            offsets = [(float(rng.uniform(-1.2, 1.2)), -0.8 * (i // 2), 0.15 * i + abs(0.1 * jt()))
                       for i in range(k)]
            out.append(_base(
                f'Group of {k}',
                f'{k} pedestrian{"s" if k > 1 else ""} cross together into the path of one '
                f'cyclist.',
                [*[ped(i + 1, p) for i, p in enumerate(group(lead, offsets))],
                 bike(k + 1, _ride(js(BIKE_SPEED), T_CONFLICT + jt()))]))
    else:
        for _ in range(n):
            n_p, n_b = int(rng.integers(1, 5)), int(rng.integers(1, 4))
            agents = []
            for i in range(n_p):
                agents.append(ped(i + 1, _cross_through(
                    (float(rng.uniform(2, 8)), float(rng.uniform(-2, 2))),
                    float(rng.uniform(55, 125)) + (180.0 if rng.random() < 0.5 else 0.0),
                    float(rng.uniform(1.1, 1.6)), float(rng.uniform(4, 9)))))
            for j in range(n_b):
                agents.append(bike(n_p + j + 1, _ride(float(rng.uniform(4, 8)),
                                                      float(rng.uniform(3, 10)),
                                                      y=float(rng.uniform(-2, 2)))))
            out.append(_base(
                f'Mixed traffic {n_p}P {n_b}B',
                f'{n_p} pedestrian{"s" if n_p > 1 else ""} and {n_b} '
                f'cyclist{"s" if n_b > 1 else ""} at random times, angles and speeds.',
                agents))
    return _finish(out, family, seed)

def get_scenario(key: str) -> dict:
    """Look up one scenario.

    ``key`` is a slug (``'fast-approach'``), an exact display name (``'Fast Approach'``) or
    ``'suite:index'`` with a zero-based index (``'conformance:7'`` is Fast Approach).
    """
    if ':' in key:
        suite, _, idx = key.partition(':')
        if idx.lstrip('-').isdigit():
            scenarios = _suite(suite)
            i = int(idx)
            if not 0 <= i < len(scenarios):
                raise KeyError(f'{key!r}: suite {suite!r} has {len(scenarios)} scenarios')
            return scenarios[i]
    for s in all_scenarios():
        if s['id'] == key or s['name'] == key:
            return s
    raise KeyError(f'no scenario with id or name {key!r}')

docs.title: schema
docs.text:
Validation of scenario dicts.

:func:validate_scenario checks one scenario against the testbench format and the library metadata; :func:validate_suites also checks that ids and names are unique across scenarios. Both return a list of human-readable problems, empty when everything is fine.

Speed and acceleration limits are per agent model and deliberately generous: they catch typos (a pedestrian at 15 m/s, a waypoint with the wrong time) rather than judge realism. Speeds are segment speeds of the piecewise-linear path in m/s; accelerations are velocity changes between consecutive segments in m/s^2, so they include turning.

docs.text:
validate_scenario(s: dict) -> list[str]

Problems found in one scenario (empty list when valid).

Source code in bikeped/scenarios/schema.py 
def validate_scenario(s: dict) -> list[str]:
    """Problems found in one scenario (empty list when valid)."""
    problems: list[str] = []
    label = s.get('id') or s.get('name') or '<unnamed>'

    def bad(msg: str) -> None:
        problems.append(f'{label}: {msg}')

    if not isinstance(s.get('name'), str) or not s.get('name'):
        bad('missing name')
    if s.get('expected_dominant') not in STATES:
        bad(f"expected_dominant {s.get('expected_dominant')!r} not one of {STATES}")
    if 'vehicle' in s and s['vehicle'] not in VEHICLES:
        bad(f"unknown vehicle {s['vehicle']!r}")
    if 'suite' in s and not isinstance(s['suite'], str):
        bad('suite must be a string')
    if 'family' in s and s['family'] not in _known_families():
        bad(f"unknown family {s['family']!r}")
    if 'tags' in s and not all(isinstance(t, str) for t in s['tags']):
        bad('tags must be strings')
    weather = (s.get('render') or {}).get('weather')
    if weather is not None and weather not in WEATHER:
        bad(f'unknown weather preset {weather!r}')
    agents = s.get('agents')
    if not isinstance(agents, list) or not agents:
        bad('needs a non-empty agents list')
        return problems
    coarse = s.get('suite') == 'conformance'
    ids = [a.get('id') for a in agents]
    if len(set(ids)) != len(ids):
        bad(f'duplicate agent ids {ids}')
    for a in agents:
        who = f"agent {a.get('id')}"
        if a.get('type') not in AGENT_TYPES:
            bad(f"{who}: type {a.get('type')!r} not one of {AGENT_TYPES}")
            continue
        model = a.get('model')
        allowed = PERSON_MODELS if a['type'] == 'person' else BIKE_MODELS
        if model is not None and model not in allowed:
            bad(f'{who}: model {model!r} not valid for a {a["type"]}')
            continue
        path = a.get('path')
        if not isinstance(path, list) or len(path) < 2:
            bad(f'{who}: path needs at least two waypoints')
            continue
        if not all(isinstance(p, dict) and all(_finite(p.get(k)) for k in 'xyt') for p in path):
            bad(f'{who}: every waypoint needs finite x, y, t')
            continue
        ts = [p['t'] for p in path]
        if any(t1 <= t0 for t0, t1 in zip(ts, ts[1:])):
            bad(f'{who}: waypoint times must be strictly increasing')
            continue
        if ts[0] < 0:
            bad(f'{who}: negative start time')
        vmax, amax = LIMITS[(a['type'], model)]
        speeds = path_speeds(path)
        if speeds.max() > vmax + 1e-6:
            bad(f'{who}: speed {speeds.max():.2f} m/s exceeds {vmax} m/s for '
                f'{model or a["type"]}')
        acc = path_accelerations(path)
        limit = amax * (COARSE_ACCEL_FACTOR if coarse else 1.0)
        if len(acc) and acc.max() > limit + 1e-6:
            bad(f'{who}: acceleration {acc.max():.2f} m/s^2 exceeds {limit} m/s^2')
    return problems

Validate every scenario and check that ids and names are unique among them.

Source code in bikeped/scenarios/schema.py 
def validate_suites(scenarios: Iterable[dict]) -> list[str]:
    """Validate every scenario and check that ids and names are unique among them."""
    problems: list[str] = []
    seen_ids: dict[str, str] = {}
    seen_names: dict[str, str] = {}
    for s in scenarios:
        problems.extend(validate_scenario(s))
        where = f"{s.get('suite', '?')}"
        sid = s.get('id')
        if not sid:
            problems.append(f"{s.get('name')}: missing id")
        elif sid in seen_ids:
            problems.append(f'duplicate id {sid!r} in {seen_ids[sid]} and {where}')
        else:
            seen_ids[sid] = where
        name = s.get('name')
        if name in seen_names:
            problems.append(f'duplicate name {name!r} in {seen_names[name]} and {where}')
        else:
            seen_names[name] = where
    return problems

Data types shared by the CARLA runtime and the imaging code.

Nothing in this module imports carla. The runtime (session, actors, rigs, runner) fills these records from the simulator, and the imaging code (projection, ground truth, overlay, recorder, export) consumes them, so both halves can be developed and tested without a server.

docs.title: Frames of reference
docs.text:
Scenario frame The frame of the testbench scenarios: metres, right-handed, x along the road (cyclists travel along it), y across the road (pedestrians cross along it), crosswalk centre at (5, 0).

World frame The CARLA world frame: metres, left-handed, x forward, y right, z up. Rotations are (pitch, yaw, roll) in degrees with the Unreal convention used by carla.Rotation.

Camera basis A camera is described by its position and by three orthonormal world-frame vectors forward, right and up. A world point P has camera coordinates (f, r, u) = (forward . d, right . d, up . d) with d = P - position. Image u grows with r and image v grows with -u.

CameraModel(
    name: str,
    kind: str,
    width: int,
    height: int,
    position: Vec3,
    forward: Vec3,
    right: Vec3,
    up: Vec3,
    fov_deg: float = 90.0,
    cx: Optional[float] = None,
    cy: Optional[float] = None,
    f_px_per_rad: Optional[float] = None,
    k1: float = 0.0,
    k2: float = 0.0,
    circle_radius_px: Optional[float] = None,
)

Intrinsics and world pose of one rendered view.

kind is "pinhole" or "fisheye".

Pinhole: fov_deg is the horizontal field of view, and the focal length in pixels is width / (2 tan(fov / 2)).

Fisheye: the optical axis is forward and the projection is the equidistant model with odd polynomial terms, r = f_px_per_rad * (theta + k1 theta^3 + k2 theta^5), where theta is the angle between the ray and the optical axis. fov_deg is the full field of view of the image circle and circle_radius_px its radius. cx and cy default to the image centre.

def carla_module() -> Any:
    """Return the ``carla`` module, importing it on first use.

    Raises ``ImportError`` with installation hints when the client is missing.
    """
    if _CARLA_OVERRIDE is not None:
        return _CARLA_OVERRIDE
    try:
        return importlib.import_module("carla")
    except ImportError as exc:
        raise ImportError(
            "The CARLA Python client is not installed. Install the wheel shipped with the "
            "server, e.g. PythonAPI/carla/dist/carla-0.9.16-*.whl for Unreal Engine 4 or "
            "carla-0.10.0-cp310-*.whl (Python 3.10) for Unreal Engine 5."

def engine_for_version(version: str) -> str:
    """Map a CARLA version string to ``ue4`` (0.9.x) or ``ue5`` (0.10.x and later)."""
    parts = version.strip().lstrip("v").split(".")
    try:
        major, minor = int(parts[0]), int(parts[1])
    except (IndexError, ValueError):
        # Development builds report a git hash; only 0.9.x builds do that on this API.
        return "ue4"
    return "ue4" if (major, minor) < (0, 10) else "ue5"

def detect_engine(client: Any) -> str:
    """Return ``ue4`` or ``ue5`` for the connected server and warn on a client mismatch."""
    server = str(client.get_server_version())
    engine = engine_for_version(server)
    client_version = str(getattr(client, "get_client_version", lambda: "")())
    if client_version and engine_for_version(client_version) != engine:
        log.warning(
            "CARLA client %s does not match server %s (%s); install %s",
            client_version, server, engine, PROFILES[engine].wheel_hint,
        )
    return engine

attribute_text(blueprint: Any, name: str) -> Optional[str]

Value of a blueprint attribute as lower-case text, or None when absent.

The real client refuses as_str() on numeric attributes, so the typed accessors are tried in turn.

Source code in bikeped/sim/engine.py 
def attribute_text(blueprint: Any, name: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """Value of a blueprint attribute as lower-case text, or ``None`` when absent.

    The real client refuses ``as_str()`` on numeric attributes, so the typed
    accessors are tried in turn.
    """
    if not blueprint.has_attribute(name):
        return None
    attribute = blueprint.get_attribute(name)
    for getter in ("as_str", "as_int", "as_float", "as_bool"):
        fn = getattr(attribute, getter, None)
        if fn is None:
            continue
        try:
            return str(fn()).lower()
        except (RuntimeError, ValueError, TypeError):
            continue
    return str(attribute).lower()

def is_two_wheeler(blueprint: Any) -> bool:

def probe(client: Any) -> Capabilities:
    """Query a connected server for maps, blueprints, sensors and world features."""
    engine = detect_engine(client)
    world = client.get_world()
    library = world.get_blueprint_library()
    caps = Capabilities(
        engine=engine,
        server_version=str(client.get_server_version()),
        client_version=str(getattr(client, "get_client_version", lambda: "")()),
        map=world.get_map().name.split("/")[-1],
        maps=sorted({m.split("/")[-1] for m in client.get_available_maps()}),
    )
    for bp in library.filter("vehicle.*"):
        if is_two_wheeler(bp):
            caps.two_wheelers.append(bp.id)
            if (_attr(bp, "base_type") or "").lower() == "bicycle":
                caps.bicycles.append(bp.id)
        else:
            caps.vehicles += 1
    for bp in library.filter("walker.pedestrian.*"):
        caps.walkers += 1
        if (_attr(bp, "can_use_wheelchair") or "").lower() == "true":
            caps.wheelchair_walkers.append(bp.id)
        if (_attr(bp, "age") or "").lower() == "child":
            caps.child_walkers.append(bp.id)
    ids = {bp.id for bp in library.filter("sensor.camera.*")}
    caps.depth_camera = "sensor.camera.depth" in ids
    caps.instance_camera = "sensor.camera.instance_segmentation" in ids
    caps.ground_projection = hasattr(world, "ground_projection")
    caps.light_manager = hasattr(world, "get_lightmanager")
    try:
        caps.crosswalks = len(world.get_map().get_crosswalks()) // 5
    except (AttributeError, RuntimeError):
        caps.crosswalks = 0
    return caps

def format_capabilities(caps: Capabilities) -> str:
    """Render capabilities as an aligned two-column table."""
    def yes(flag: bool) -> str:
        return "yes" if flag else "no"

    rows = [
        ("engine", caps.engine),
        ("server version", caps.server_version),
        ("client version", caps.client_version),
        ("current map", caps.map),
        ("maps", ", ".join(caps.maps)),
        ("two-wheelers", ", ".join(caps.two_wheelers) or "none (cyclists need --cyclist-proxy)"),
        ("bicycles", ", ".join(caps.bicycles) or "none"),
        ("walkers", f"{caps.walkers} ({len(caps.child_walkers)} child, "
                    f"{len(caps.wheelchair_walkers)} wheelchair-capable)"),
        ("four-wheeled vehicles", str(caps.vehicles)),
        ("depth camera", yes(caps.depth_camera)),
        ("instance segmentation", yes(caps.instance_camera)),
        ("ground projection", yes(caps.ground_projection)),
        ("light manager", yes(caps.light_manager)),
        ("crosswalks on map", str(caps.crosswalks)),
    ]
    width = max(len(k) for k, _ in rows)
    return "\n".join(f"{k.ljust(width)}  {v}" for k, v in rows)

docs.text:
Locate, launch and stop a CARLA server process.

A CARLA release ships a launcher script (CarlaUE4.sh in the Unreal Engine 4 releases, CarlaUnreal.sh in the Unreal Engine 5 release) that starts the simulator binary. This module finds an install, builds the launch command for either engine, runs it in its own process group, waits until a client can read the server version and stops the whole group again.

carla is only needed by :meth:ServerProcess.wait_ready, which asks the server for its version through a client.

def start(self) -> "ServerProcess":
    """Launch the server and return immediately.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: a server was already started from this object, or
            something already listens on the RPC port.
        FileNotFoundError: no install with the engine's launcher was found.
    """
    if self._process is not None:
        raise RuntimeError("this server was already started")
    if _port_open(self.host, self.port):
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"port {self.port} on {self.host} is already in use; stop the server that "
            "listens there or choose another --port"
        )
    root = find_install(self.engine, self.root)
    self.command = build_command(
        self.engine, root, self.port, self.quality, self.windowed, self.extra_args
    )
    self.log_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    log = open(self.log_path, "wb")
    try:
        self._process = subprocess.Popen(
            self.command,
            cwd=str(Path(self.command[0]).parent),
            stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stdout=log,
            stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
            start_new_session=True,
        )
    except OSError:
        log.close()
        raise
    self._log = log
    # start_new_session makes the launcher the leader of a new process group.
    self._pgid = self._process.pid
    logger.info("started CARLA %s server (pid %d): %s", self.engine, self._process.pid,
                " ".join(self.command))
    return self

def wait_ready(self, timeout: float = 180.0, poll_interval: float = 1.0) -> str:
    """Block until a client can read the server version, and return it.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: the server was not started or exited while starting up.
        TimeoutError: the server did not answer within ``timeout`` seconds.
    """
    if self._process is None:
        raise RuntimeError("the server has not been started")
    carla = carla_module()
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    last_error: Optional[Exception] = None
    while True:
        if not self.running:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"the CARLA server exited with code {self._process.returncode} before it "
                f"accepted connections; its output is in {self.log_path}\n{self.log_tail()}"
            )
        try:
            client = carla.Client(self.host, self.port)
            client.set_timeout(2.0)
            self.version = str(client.get_server_version())
            logger.info("CARLA server %s is ready on port %d", self.version, self.port)
            return self.version
        except (RuntimeError, OSError) as error:
            last_error = error
        remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
        if remaining <= 0.0:
            raise TimeoutError(
                f"no answer from the CARLA server on {self.host}:{self.port} after "
                f"{timeout:.0f} s (last error: {last_error}); its output is in {self.log_path}"
            )
        time.sleep(min(poll_interval, remaining))

The process group receives SIGTERM and, if it is still alive after grace seconds, SIGKILL. Calling this on a server that is not running does nothing.

Source code in bikeped/sim/server.py 
def stop(self, grace: float = 10.0) -> None:
    """Stop the server and every process it started.

    The process group receives ``SIGTERM`` and, if it is still alive after
    ``grace`` seconds, ``SIGKILL``. Calling this on a server that is not
    running does nothing.
    """
    if self._process is None:
        return
    try:
        if self.running:
            self._signal_group(signal.SIGTERM)
            if not self._wait_exit(grace):
                logger.warning("CARLA server ignored SIGTERM for %.0f s, killing it", grace)
                self._signal_group(signal.SIGKILL)
                if not self._wait_exit(grace):
                    logger.error("CARLA server process group %s is still alive", self._pgid)
    finally:
        if self._log is not None:
            self._log.close()
            self._log = None
        self._process = None
        self._pgid = None

def launcher_path(engine: str, root: PathLike) -> Path:
    """Path of the launcher script inside the install at ``root``.

    The UE4 archives keep the launcher at the top of the install and the UE5
    archive keeps it under ``Linux/``, so both places are checked. When the
    script is in neither, the top-level path is returned so that callers can
    name it in their error message.
    """
    profile = _profile(engine)
    base = Path(root).expanduser()
    candidates = (base / profile.launcher, base / "Linux" / profile.launcher)
    for candidate in candidates:
        if candidate.is_file():
            return candidate
    return candidates[0]

def find_install(engine: str, root: Optional[PathLike] = None) -> Path:
    """Return the root folder of a CARLA install for ``engine``.

    An explicit ``root`` is the only place searched when it is given. Without
    it, the engine's environment variable (``CARLA_UE4_ROOT`` or
    ``CARLA_UE5_ROOT``) is tried first and then the profile's list of common
    install paths.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: no candidate contains the engine's launcher script.
    """
    profile = _profile(engine)
    if root is not None:
        base = Path(root).expanduser()
        if launcher_path(engine, base).is_file():
            return base
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"{profile.launcher} not found in {base} or {base / 'Linux'}. Point --root or "
            f"{profile.root_env} at the folder of the extracted CARLA release."
        )

    candidates: List[str] = []
    env_root = os.environ.get(profile.root_env)
    if env_root:
        candidates.append(env_root)
    candidates.extend(profile.search_paths)

    tried: List[str] = []
    for candidate in candidates:
        base = Path(os.path.expandvars(candidate)).expanduser()
        if launcher_path(engine, base).is_file():
            return base
        tried.append(str(base))
    looked = ", ".join(tried) if tried else "no candidate paths"
    raise FileNotFoundError(
        f"No CARLA {engine} install found (looked for {profile.launcher} in: {looked}). "
        f"Set {profile.root_env} or pass --root with the folder of the extracted CARLA release."
    )

def build_command(
    engine: str,
    root: Optional[PathLike] = None,
    port: int = 2000,
    quality: str = "Epic",
    windowed: bool = False,
    extra_args: Sequence[str] = (),
) -> List[str]:
    """Build the argument list that launches a server.

    The server renders off screen unless ``windowed`` is set. ``port`` is the
    RPC port; the server also uses the two ports after it for streaming.
    ``quality`` is passed as ``-quality-level=`` on UE4 and ignored on UE5,
    whose launcher has no such flag. With ``root`` left out the install is
    looked up with :func:`find_install`.
    """
    profile = _profile(engine)
    level = _quality(quality)
    base = find_install(engine) if root is None else root
    command = [str(launcher_path(engine, base))]
    for flag in profile.launch_flags:
        if windowed and flag.lower() == "-renderoffscreen":
            continue
        command.append(flag)
    if windowed:
        command.append("-windowed")
    command.append(f"-carla-rpc-port={int(port)}")
    if profile.supports_quality_flag:
        command.append(f"-quality-level={level}")
    command.extend(extra_args)
    return command

@contextlib.contextmanager
def managed_server(
    engine: str,
    root: Optional[PathLike] = None,
    port: int = 2000,
    quality: str = "Epic",
    windowed: bool = False,
    timeout: float = 180.0,
    host: str = "127.0.0.1",
    log_path: Optional[PathLike] = None,
) -> Iterator[ServerProcess]:
    """Run a CARLA server for the duration of a ``with`` block.

    The server is started, the block is entered once a client can reach it,
    and the server is stopped when the block exits for any reason, including
    an exception or a keyboard interrupt.
    """
    server = ServerProcess(
        engine, root=root, port=port, quality=quality, windowed=windowed, host=host,
        log_path=log_path,
    )
    try:
        server.start()
        server.wait_ready(timeout=timeout)
        yield server
    finally:
        server.stop()

def collect(self, frame: int) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Decoded data of every sensor for ``frame``."""
    out: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    deadline = time.monotonic() + self.timeout
    for key, q in self._queues.items():
        while True:
            remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
            try:
                data = q.get(timeout=max(remaining, 0.001))
            except queue.Empty:
                raise TimeoutError(
                    f"sensor '{key}' delivered nothing for frame {frame} within "
                    f"{self.timeout:.0f} s; the server may be overloaded (try --quality draft "
                    "or fewer views)") from None
            if data.frame == frame:
                out[key] = self._decoders[key](data)
                break
            if data.frame > frame:
                raise RuntimeError(f"sensor '{key}' skipped frame {frame} (got {data.frame})")
    return out

def traffic_manager(self) -> Any:

def destroy(self, actor: Any) -> None:
    """Destroy one tracked actor now and stop tracking it."""

def close(self) -> None:
    """Stop sensors, destroy tracked actors, restore settings. Safe to call twice."""
    for sensor in reversed(self.sensors):
        try:
            if getattr(sensor, "is_listening", False):
                sensor.stop()
        except RuntimeError:
            pass
    for actor in reversed(self.sensors + self.actors):
        try:
            if getattr(actor, "is_alive", True):
                actor.destroy()
        except RuntimeError as exc:
            log.debug("destroy %s failed: %s", getattr(actor, "id", "?"), exc)
    self.sensors, self.actors = [], []
    if self.hidden_objects and self.world is not None:
        try:
            self.world.enable_environment_objects(set(self.hidden_objects), True)
        except RuntimeError as exc:
            log.warning("could not restore hidden map objects: %s", exc)
        self.hidden_objects = set()
    if self._tm is not None:
        try:
            self._tm.set_synchronous_mode(False)
        except RuntimeError:
            pass
        self._tm = None
    if self.world is not None and self._original_settings is not None:
        try:
            self.world.apply_settings(self._original_settings)
        except RuntimeError as exc:
            log.warning("could not restore world settings: %s", exc)
        self._original_settings = None

def depth_to_metres(image: Any) -> np.ndarray:
    """Decode a ``sensor.camera.depth`` image to ``float32`` metres (1000 m far plane)."""
    buf = np.frombuffer(image.raw_data, dtype=np.uint8).reshape(image.height, image.width, 4)
    b, g, r = (buf[:, :, i].astype(np.float32) for i in range(3))
    return ((r + g * 256.0 + b * 65536.0) / (256.0 ** 3 - 1.0) * 1000.0).astype(np.float32)

docs.title: site
docs.text:
Placement of the scenario frame on a CARLA crosswalk.

The scenario frame (see :mod:bikeped.sim.types) is anchored on one crosswalk: scenario +y runs along the crosswalk (the direction pedestrians cross), scenario +x runs along the road, and the crosswalk centre is scenario (5, 0). As in the original carla_scenario.py, the reference short edge of the crosswalk polygon defines -y (the pole stands there). The road axis is the cross axis turned by (a, b) -> (-b, a) in world coordinates: the world frame is left-handed, so this is the choice that keeps the scene unmirrored (seen from above, turning from scenario +x to +y is a counter-clockwise turn in both frames, and a cyclist approaching from scenario +x enters the pole view from the right, as in the testbench camera).

Everything here is plain numpy. :meth:Site.from_world is the only method that touches a CARLA world, and only through world.get_map().get_crosswalks().

@classmethod
def from_crosswalk(cls, entry: Dict[str, Any]) -> "Site":
    """Build a site from one ``crosswalks.json`` entry (``corners``, ``center``)."""
    corners = [np.asarray(c[:2], dtype=np.float64) for c in entry["corners"]]
    edges = []
    for i in range(4):
        a, b = corners[i], corners[(i + 1) % 4]
        edges.append((float(np.linalg.norm(b - a)), (a + b) / 2.0))
    edges.sort(key=lambda e: e[0])
    cam_edge = edges[0][1]
    center3 = list(entry["center"])
    center = np.asarray(center3[:2], dtype=np.float64)
    to_center = center - cam_edge
    half = float(np.linalg.norm(to_center))
    cross = to_center / half
    road = np.array([-cross[1], cross[0]])
    origin = center - 5.0 * road
    px, py, ph = _testbench_pole()
    return cls(
        origin=(float(origin[0]), float(origin[1])),
        road_axis=(float(road[0]), float(road[1])),
        cross_axis=(float(cross[0]), float(cross[1])),
        ground_z=float(center3[2]) if len(center3) > 2 else 0.0,
        road_half_width=half,
        crosswalk_id=entry.get("id"),
        pole_xy=(px, py),
        pole_height=ph,
    )

@classmethod
def from_world(cls, world: Any, index: int) -> "Site":
    """Build a site from crosswalk ``index`` of the loaded map.

    ``Map.get_crosswalks()`` returns closed polygons as a flat list of
    locations; rectangles come with their first point repeated (five points).
    """
    entries = crosswalks_from_points(
        [(p.x, p.y, p.z) for p in world.get_map().get_crosswalks()])
    if not entries:
        raise RuntimeError("the loaded map exposes no crosswalk polygons")
    if not 0 <= index < len(entries):
        raise IndexError(f"crosswalk {index} not found, the map has {len(entries)}")
    return cls.from_crosswalk(entries[index])

def to_world(self, x: float, y: float, z: float = 0.0) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:
    """Scenario ``(x, y)`` and height above ground to world ``(X, Y, Z)``."""
    X = self.origin[0] + x * self.road_axis[0] + y * self.cross_axis[0]
    Y = self.origin[1] + x * self.road_axis[1] + y * self.cross_axis[1]
    return float(X), float(Y), float(self.ground_z + z)

def heading_to_yaw(self, heading: float) -> float:
    """Scenario heading (radians, 0 = +x) to CARLA yaw (degrees, clockwise from above)."""
    dx = math.cos(heading) * self.road_axis[0] + math.sin(heading) * self.cross_axis[0]
    dy = math.cos(heading) * self.road_axis[1] + math.sin(heading) * self.cross_axis[1]
    return math.degrees(math.atan2(dy, dx))

def yaw_to_heading(self, yaw_deg: float) -> float:
    """Inverse of :meth:`heading_to_yaw`."""
    c, s = math.cos(math.radians(yaw_deg)), math.sin(math.radians(yaw_deg))
    x = c * self.road_axis[0] + s * self.road_axis[1]
    y = c * self.cross_axis[0] + s * self.cross_axis[1]
    return math.atan2(y, x)
