    """World-frame unit vector (X, Y, 0) of a scenario heading."""
    yaw = math.radians(self.heading_to_yaw(heading))
    return np.array([math.cos(yaw), math.sin(yaw), 0.0])

docs.title: crosswalks_from_points
docs.text:
crosswalks_from_points(points: Sequence[Tuple[float, float, float]]) -> list

Split CARLA's flat crosswalk point list into crosswalks.json-like entries.

A polygon ends where a point repeats the polygon's first point. Polygons with other than four distinct corners are approximated by their minimum-area rectangle so the edge logic of :meth:Site.from_crosswalk applies.

Source code in bikeped/sim/site.py 
def crosswalks_from_points(points: Sequence[Tuple[float, float, float]]) -> list:
    """Split CARLA's flat crosswalk point list into ``crosswalks.json``-like entries.

    A polygon ends where a point repeats the polygon's first point. Polygons with
    other than four distinct corners are approximated by their minimum-area
    rectangle so the edge logic of :meth:`Site.from_crosswalk` applies.
    """
    entries = []
    current: list = []
    for p in points:
        if current and np.allclose(p[:2], current[0][:2], atol=1e-3):
            entries.append(current)
            current = []
        else:
            current.append(tuple(float(v) for v in p))
    out = []
    for poly in entries:
        if len(poly) < 3:
            continue
        pts = np.asarray(poly, dtype=np.float64)
        corners = pts[:, :2] if len(poly) == 4 else _min_area_rect(pts[:, :2])
        z = float(pts[:, 2].mean())
        center = corners.mean(axis=0)
        out.append({
            "id": len(out),
            "center": [float(center[0]), float(center[1]), z],
            "corners": [[float(c[0]), float(c[1]), z] for c in corners],
        })
    return out

Smooth rendering poses for scripted scenario agents.

Positions come straight from the scripted piecewise-linear path with the same semantics as decision_testbench.interpolate_agent, so the ground truth stays exact. Rendering trajectory of one scenario agent sampled on a fixed time grid.

def __init__(self, agent: Dict[str, Any], fps: int = 30, time_constant: Optional[float] = None,
             max_turn_rate: Optional[float] = None) -> None:
    self.agent = agent
    self.id = int(agent["id"])
    self.kind = str(agent["type"])
    path = agent["path"]
    self.t = np.array([float(p["t"]) for p in path])
    self.xy = np.array([[float(p["x"]), float(p["y"])] for p in path])
    self.fps = int(fps)
    bike = self.kind == "bike"
    self.time_constant = time_constant if time_constant is not None else (0.35 if bike else 0.2)
    self.max_turn_rate = max_turn_rate if max_turn_rate is not None else (1.6 if bike else 4.0)
    self._grid, self._heading, self._rate = self._filter_headings()

Scripted position, clamped to the path ends outside the active window.

Source code in bikeped/sim/motion.py 
def position(self, t: float) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    """Scripted position, clamped to the path ends outside the active window."""
    if len(self.t) == 1:
        return float(self.xy[0, 0]), float(self.xy[0, 1])
    tc = min(max(t, self.start), self.end)
    i = self._segment(tc)
    span = self.t[i + 1] - self.t[i]
    frac = 0.0 if span <= 0 else (tc - self.t[i]) / span
    p = self.xy[i] + (self.xy[i + 1] - self.xy[i]) * frac
    return float(p[0]), float(p[1])

def velocity(self, t: float) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    """Velocity (m/s) of the segment containing ``t``; zero outside the window."""
    if len(self.t) == 1 or not self.active(t):
        return 0.0, 0.0
    i = self._segment(t)
    span = self.t[i + 1] - self.t[i]
    if span <= 0:
        return 0.0, 0.0
    v = (self.xy[i + 1] - self.xy[i]) / span
    return float(v[0]), float(v[1])

Heading of the segment containing t (what interpolate_agent reports).

Source code in bikeped/sim/motion.py 
def path_heading(self, t: float) -> float:
    """Heading of the segment containing ``t`` (what ``interpolate_agent`` reports)."""
    if len(self.t) == 1:
        return 0.0
    i = self._segment(min(max(t, self.start), self.end))
    d = self.xy[i + 1] - self.xy[i]
    if not np.any(d):
        for j in list(range(i, -1, -1)) + list(range(i + 1, len(self.t) - 1)):
            d = self.xy[j + 1] - self.xy[j]
            if np.any(d):
                break
    return float(math.atan2(d[1], d[0]))

def heading(self, t: float) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    """Smoothed heading (rad) and yaw rate (rad/s) at ``t``."""

def sample(self, t: float) -> Pose:
    """Full pose at time ``t``."""
    x, y = self.position(t)
    vx, vy = self.velocity(t)
    speed = math.hypot(vx, vy)
    heading, rate = self.heading(t)
    lean = 0.0
    if self.kind == "bike":
        lean = float(np.clip(math.atan(speed * rate / GRAVITY), -MAX_LEAN_RAD, MAX_LEAN_RAD))
    return Pose(t=t, active=self.active(t), x=x, y=y, vx=vx, vy=vy, speed=speed,
                path_heading=self.path_heading(t), heading=heading, yaw_rate=rate, lean=lean)

docs.title: actors
docs.text:
Spawning and driving the scripted scenario agents.

Each scenario agent becomes one CARLA actor (a walker for person agents, a two-wheeled vehicle for bike agents, or a walker standing in for a cyclist when the engine has no rideable two-wheeler and cyclist_proxy='walker').

Two drive modes are available:

kinematic The actor is placed on the scripted pose every tick. Height comes from a ground profile sampled with world.ground_projection before any actor exists (so the ray never hits an agent), yaw from the smoothed heading and, for two-wheelers, roll from the lean angle. Walkers keep physics and also receive a WalkerControl so their walk cycle plays.

velocity Walkers are steered with WalkerControl (scripted velocity plus a proportional correction on position error) and riders with target linear and angular velocities plus a light throttle and steer so wheels, pedals and handlebar move. An actor is re-placed on its scripted pose only when the position error exceeds a tolerance.

Positions reported to the decision pipeline and the ground truth always come from the script, never from the simulated actor.

def __init__(self, session: Any, site: Site, scenario: Dict[str, Any],
             trajectories: Sequence[Trajectory], caps: Capabilities, *,
             drive: str = "kinematic",
             seed: int = 0, cyclist_proxy: Optional[str] = None,
             walker_drive: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
    if drive not in DRIVE_MODES:
        raise ValueError(f"drive must be one of {DRIVE_MODES}")
    self.session = session
    self.site = site
    self.scenario = scenario
    self.caps = caps
    self.drive = drive
    self.walker_drive = walker_drive or drive
    self.rng = random.Random(seed)
    self.cyclist_proxy = cyclist_proxy
    self.agents: List[Agent] = []
    self.dt = session.fixed_delta
    self.time = 0.0
    if needs_rideable(scenario) and not caps.has_rideable and cyclist_proxy != "walker":
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"{caps.engine} server {caps.server_version} has no rideable two-wheeler "
            "blueprint, so cyclists cannot be rendered. Pass --cyclist-proxy walker to "
            "render them as walkers.")
    defs = {int(a["id"]): a for a in scenario["agents"]}
    for traj in trajectories:
        a = defs[traj.id]
        model = str(a.get("model") or ("bicycle" if a["type"] == "bike" else "adult"))
        self.agents.append(Agent(trajectory=traj, kind=a["type"], model=model))

sample_ground(step: float = 0.5) -> None

Sample ground heights along every path before any agent is spawned.

Source code in bikeped/sim/actors.py 
def sample_ground(self, step: float = 0.5) -> None:
    """Sample ground heights along every path before any agent is spawned."""
    world = self.session.world
    carla = self.session.carla
    for agent in self.agents:
        traj = agent.trajectory
        pts: List[Tuple[float, float, float]] = []
        t = traj.start
        while t <= traj.end + 1e-9:
            x, y = traj.position(t)
            pts.append((x, y, self._project(world, carla, x, y)))
            t += step / max(1.0, math.hypot(*traj.velocity(t)) or 1.0)
        agent.ground = pts

spawn() -> None

Choose the blueprint of every agent; actors appear when their window starts.

Actors are spawned on their first active tick and destroyed after their last one. Parking inactive actors under the map is not an option: walkers keep falling with physics disabled and the engine deletes them at the kill height.

Source code in bikeped/sim/actors.py 
def spawn(self) -> None:
    """Choose the blueprint of every agent; actors appear when their window starts.

    Actors are spawned on their first active tick and destroyed after their
    last one. Parking inactive actors under the map is not an option: walkers
    keep falling with physics disabled and the engine deletes them at the
    kill height.
    """
    library = self.session.world.get_blueprint_library()
    for agent in self.agents:
        bp = None
        if agent.kind == "bike" and self.caps.has_rideable:
            bp = choose_rider(library, agent.model, self.rng)
        if bp is None:
            walker_model = agent.model if agent.model in WALKER_MODELS else "adult"
            bp, wheelchair = choose_walker(library, walker_model, self.rng)
            if wheelchair and bp.has_attribute("use_wheelchair"):
                bp.set_attribute("use_wheelchair", "true")
            if bp.has_attribute("is_invincible"):
                bp.set_attribute("is_invincible", "false")
            agent.walker = True
            if agent.kind == "bike":
                agent.model = f"walker-proxy:{agent.model}"
        else:
            agent.walker = False
        if bp.has_attribute("role_name"):
            bp.set_attribute("role_name", f"scripted_{agent.trajectory.id}")
        agent.bp, agent.blueprint = bp, bp.id

def drive_tick(self, t: float) -> None:
    """Command every actor for the step that ends at ``t``."""
    self.time = t
    for agent in self.agents:
        traj = agent.trajectory
        active = traj.active(t)
        if not active:
            if agent.visible:
                self._hide(agent)
            continue
        if not agent.visible:
            self._show(agent, t)
            continue
        mode = self.walker_drive if agent.walker else self.drive
        if mode == "kinematic":
            self._drive_kinematic(agent, t)
        else:
            self._drive_velocity(agent, t)

Source code in bikeped/sim/actors.py 
def states(self, t: float, scripted: Dict[int, Dict[str, Any]]) -> List[AgentState]:
    """``AgentState`` of every agent active at ``t`` from the actual actor pose."""
    import decision_testbench as tb

    out: List[AgentState] = []
    for agent in self.agents:
        pos = scripted.get(agent.trajectory.id)
        if pos is None or agent.actor is None:
            continue
        tf = agent.actor.get_transform()
        bb = agent.actor.bounding_box
        ext = (float(bb.extent.x), float(bb.extent.y), float(bb.extent.z))
        centre = tf.transform(bb.location)
        loc = (float(centre.x), float(centre.y), float(centre.z))
        if agent.kind == "bike" and not agent.walker and min(ext[0], ext[2]) < 0.3:
            obj = tb.OBJECT_TYPES["cyclist"]
            ext = (obj.length / 2.0, obj.width / 2.0, obj.height / 2.0)
            gz = self.ground_z(agent, pos["x"], pos["y"])
            loc = (float(tf.location.x), float(tf.location.y), gz + obj.height / 2.0)
        rot = (float(tf.rotation.pitch), float(tf.rotation.yaw), float(tf.rotation.roll))
        sx, sy = self.site.to_scenario(tf.location.x, tf.location.y)
        vx, vy = agent.trajectory.velocity(t)
        out.append(AgentState(
            id=agent.trajectory.id, kind=agent.kind, sx=float(pos["x"]), sy=float(pos["y"]),
            heading=float(pos["heading"]), speed=math.hypot(vx, vy), location=loc,
            rotation=rot, extent=ext, model=agent.model, blueprint=agent.blueprint,
            track_error_m=math.hypot(sx - pos["x"], sy - pos["y"]),
            instance_id=int(agent.actor.id)))
    return out

Pick a walker blueprint for a hint; returns (blueprint, use_wheelchair).

def choose_walker(library: Any, model: str, rng: random.Random) -> Tuple[Any, bool]:
    """Pick a walker blueprint for a hint; returns (blueprint, use_wheelchair)."""
    walkers = sorted(library.filter("walker.pedestrian.*"), key=lambda b: b.id)
    if not walkers:
        raise RuntimeError("the server has no walker blueprints")
    adults = [b for b in walkers if _attr(b, "age") not in ("child",)]
    pool = adults or walkers
    wheelchair = False
    if model == "child":
        pool = [b for b in walkers if _attr(b, "age") == "child"] or pool
    elif model == "wheelchair":
        capable = [b for b in walkers if _attr(b, "can_use_wheelchair") == "true"]
        if capable:
            pool, wheelchair = capable, True
    return rng.choice(pool), wheelchair

def choose_rider(library: Any, model: str, rng: random.Random) -> Optional[Any]:
    """Pick a two-wheeler blueprint for a hint, or ``None`` when the engine has none."""
    rideable = sorted((b for b in library.filter("vehicle.*") if is_two_wheeler(b)),
                      key=lambda b: b.id)
    if not rideable:
        return None
    by_id = {b.id: b for b in rideable}
    for bp_id in RIDER_BLUEPRINTS.get(model or "bicycle", RIDER_BLUEPRINTS["bicycle"]):
        if bp_id in by_id:
            return by_id[bp_id]
    bicycles = [b for b in rideable if _attr(b, "base_type") == "bicycle"]
    return rng.choice(bicycles or rideable)

def weather_values(preset: str, view_yaw_deg: float) -> Dict[str, float]:
    """``WeatherParameters`` fields for ``preset`` with an absolute sun azimuth."""
    if preset not in WEATHER_PRESETS:
        raise KeyError(f"unknown weather preset '{preset}', choose from "

    values = {k: float(v) for k, v in WEATHER_PRESETS[preset].items() if k not in _META_KEYS}

    return values

def apply_weather(world: Any, preset: str, view_yaw_deg: float) -> Dict[str, float]:
    """Apply a preset field by field; returns the fields that were set."""
    weather = world.get_weather()
    applied: Dict[str, float] = {}
    for key, value in weather_values(preset, view_yaw_deg).items():
        if hasattr(weather, key):
            setattr(weather, key, value)
            applied[key] = value
    world.set_weather(weather)
    set_street_lights(world, is_night(preset))
    return applied

def set_street_lights(world: Any, on: bool) -> bool:
    """Switch street lights through the light manager when the server has one."""
    if not hasattr(world, "get_lightmanager"):
        return False
    try:
        carla = carla_module()
        manager = world.get_lightmanager()
        group = getattr(getattr(carla, "LightGroup", None), "Street", None)
        lights = manager.get_all_lights(group) if group is not None else manager.get_all_lights()
        if on:
            manager.turn_on(lights)
        else:
            manager.turn_off(lights)
        return True
    except (RuntimeError, AttributeError, TypeError) as exc:
        log.warning("street lights unavailable: %s", exc)
        return False

docs.text:
Background traffic and pedestrians around a scripted scenario.

Ambient actors make the rendered street look inhabited without getting in the way of the scripted agents. The scripted corridor is the bounding box of all scripted paths in the scenario frame plus a margin. Vehicles are spawned outside it, drive under the Traffic Manager and are stopped when they approach it. Walkers are spawned on the navigation mesh outside it, do not cross the road, and are sent back to where they started if they wander in.

The corridor helpers are plain numpy and need no simulator.

    self,
    session: Any,
    site: Any,
    scenario: Dict[str, Any],
    level: str = "none",
    seed: int = 0,

    """Stop the walker controllers. The session destroys the actors."""

def corridor_bounds(scenario: Dict[str, Any], margin: float = 6.0) -> Bounds:
    """Bounding box of every scripted path point, grown by ``margin`` metres.

    Returns ``(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax)`` in the scenario frame.
    """
    points = np.array(
        [(p["x"], p["y"]) for agent in scenario.get("agents", []) for p in agent["path"]],
        dtype=np.float64,
    )
    if points.size == 0:
        raise ValueError("the scenario has no path points to build a corridor from")
    low = points.min(axis=0) - margin
    high = points.max(axis=0) + margin
    return float(low[0]), float(low[1]), float(high[0]), float(high[1])

def distance_to_bounds(x: float, y: float, bounds: Bounds) -> float:
    """Distance in metres from ``(x, y)`` to ``bounds``, zero inside."""
    xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax = bounds
    dx = max(xmin - x, 0.0, x - xmax)
    dy = max(ymin - y, 0.0, y - ymax)
    return float(np.hypot(dx, dy))

def look_at(position: Sequence[float], target: Sequence[float]) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    """CARLA ``(pitch, yaw)`` in degrees of a level-horizon camera aimed at ``target``."""
    d = np.asarray(target, dtype=float) - np.asarray(position, dtype=float)
    yaw = math.degrees(math.atan2(d[1], d[0]))
    pitch = math.degrees(math.atan2(d[2], math.hypot(d[0], d[1])))
    return pitch, yaw

docs.text:
pole_framing(
    site: Site, scenario: Dict[str, Any], aspect: float = 16 / 9, reach_m: float = 40.0
) -> Tuple[float, float, float]

Heading (rad, scenario frame), pitch (deg) and horizontal FOV (deg) of the pole view.

The view always contains the crosswalk (scenario x = 5, |y| <= 4) and every path point within reach_m of the pole.

Source code in bikeped/sim/rigs.py 
def pole_framing(site: Site, scenario: Dict[str, Any], aspect: float = 16 / 9,
                 reach_m: float = 40.0) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:
    """Heading (rad, scenario frame), pitch (deg) and horizontal FOV (deg) of the pole view.

    The view always contains the crosswalk (scenario ``x = 5``, ``|y| <= 4``) and
    every path point within ``reach_m`` of the pole.
    """
    px, py = site.pole_xy
    pts = scenario_points(scenario)
    pts = np.vstack([pts, [[5.0, -4.0], [5.0, 4.0], [3.0, 0.0], [7.0, 0.0]]])
    d = pts - np.array([px, py])
    dist = np.hypot(d[:, 0], d[:, 1])
    d = d[(dist < reach_m) & (dist > 2.0)]
    centre = math.pi / 2.0
    angles = np.arctan2(d[:, 1], d[:, 0]) - centre
    angles = (angles + math.pi) % (2 * math.pi) - math.pi
    lo, hi = float(angles.min()), float(angles.max())
    heading = centre + (lo + hi) / 2.0
    fov = float(np.clip(math.degrees(hi - lo) + 14.0, 60.0, 100.0))
    near = float(np.percentile(np.hypot(d[:, 0], d[:, 1]), 50))
    pitch = -math.degrees(math.atan2(site.pole_height - 1.0, max(near, 4.0)))
    return heading, pitch, fov

             fps: int = 30) -> Rig:
    """Build the rig called ``name`` (one of :data:`RIG_NAMES`)."""

def resolve_scenario(ref: str, suite: Optional[str] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Look a scenario up by slug, name, ``suite:index`` or conformance index."""
    try:
        from bikeped.scenarios import get_scenario
    except ImportError:
        get_scenario = None
    if get_scenario is not None:
        key = f"{suite}:{ref}" if suite and ref.isdigit() else ref
        try:
            return get_scenario(key)
        except (KeyError, ValueError, IndexError):
            if not ref.isdigit():
                raise
    import decision_testbench as tb

    if ref.split(":")[-1].isdigit():
        return tb.SCENARIOS[int(ref.split(":")[-1])]
    for sc in tb.SCENARIOS:
        if sc["name"] == ref:
            return sc
    raise KeyError(f"unknown scenario '{ref}'")

def clear_near_field(world: Any, carla: Any, cam: Any, radius_m: float = 7.5) -> list:
    """Hide street furniture poles standing right in front of the pole camera.

    The camera is mounted on a pole of its own; a lamp post a few metres in
    front of it would cover a large part of the image. Returns the ids of the
    disabled objects so they can be enabled again.
    """
    label = getattr(getattr(carla, "CityObjectLabel", None), "Poles", None)
    if label is None or not hasattr(world, "get_environment_objects"):
        return []
    px, py, _ = cam.position
    fx, fy = cam.forward[0], cam.forward[1]
    ids = []
    for obj in world.get_environment_objects(label):
        loc = obj.transform.location
        dx, dy = loc.x - px, loc.y - py
        if math.hypot(dx, dy) < radius_m and dx * fx + dy * fy > -0.5:
            ids.append(obj.id)
    if ids:
        world.enable_environment_objects(set(ids), False)
    return ids

def render_scenario(scenario: Dict[str, Any], opts: RenderOptions,
                    recorder_factory: Optional[Callable[..., Any]] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Render ``scenario`` on a running server; returns the recorder's summary."""
    import decision_testbench as tb

    fps = opts.fps
    dt = 1.0 / fps
    trajs = trajectories(scenario, fps)
    duration = tb.get_scenario_duration(scenario)
    n_frames = int(math.floor(duration * fps + 1e-9)) + 1
    if opts.max_frames is not None:
        n_frames = min(n_frames, opts.max_frames)
    weather = opts.weather or scenario.get("render", {}).get("weather") or "clear_noon"
    recorder_factory = recorder_factory or default_recorder_factory()

    with Session(opts.host, opts.port, map_name=opts.map, fixed_delta=dt,
                 seed=opts.seed) as session:
        if opts.engine != "auto" and opts.engine != session.engine:
            raise RuntimeError(f"--engine {opts.engine} requested but the server is "
                               f"{session.engine}")
        caps = probe(session.client)
        drive = opts.drive or PROFILES[session.engine].default_drive
        site = _load_site(session, opts)
        cast = Cast(session, site, scenario, trajs, caps, drive=drive, seed=opts.seed,
                    cyclist_proxy=opts.cyclist_proxy, walker_drive=opts.extra.get("walker_drive"))
        cast.sample_ground()
        view_yaw = site.heading_to_yaw(math.pi / 2.0)
        apply_weather(session.world, weather, view_yaw)
        ambient = None
        if opts.ambient != "none":
            from .ambient import Ambient
            ambient = Ambient(session, site, scenario, level=opts.ambient, seed=opts.seed,
                              night=is_night(weather))
            ambient.spawn()
        cast.spawn()
        hub = SensorHub(timeout=30.0)
        rigs = [make_rig(name, site, scenario, opts.quality,
                         ground_truth=opts.ground_truth and name == "pole",
                         trajectories=trajs, fps=fps) for name in opts.rigs]
        for rig in rigs:
            rig.post_overrides = camera_overrides(weather)
            rig.spawn(session, hub, caps)
        if "pole" in opts.rigs:
            pole_cam = next(r for r in rigs if r.name == "pole").camera(0.0)
            session.hidden_objects.update(
                clear_near_field(session.world, session.carla, pole_cam))
        warm = max(int(opts.warmup_s * fps), settle_ticks(weather, fps))
        for _ in range(warm):
            if ambient is not None:
                ambient.tick()
            frame_id = session.tick()
            hub.collect(frame_id)

        run = RunInfo(
            scenario_name=scenario["name"], scenario_id=scenario_slug(scenario),
            suite=str(scenario.get("suite", "conformance")), fps=fps, duration_s=duration,
            engine=session.engine, server_version=caps.server_version,
            client_version=caps.client_version, map=caps.map, crosswalk_id=opts.crosswalk,
            weather=weather, quality=opts.quality, drive=drive, ambient=opts.ambient,
            seed=opts.seed, views=list(opts.rigs), site=site.to_dict(),
            pipeline_config=opts.pipeline_config,
            extra={"cyclist_proxy": opts.cyclist_proxy, **opts.extra})
        recorder = recorder_factory(Path(opts.out), run, views=list(opts.rigs),
                                    overlay=opts.overlay,
                                    layout=opts.layout, save_frames=opts.save_frames,
                                    scenario=scenario)
        pipeline = tb.make_pipeline(tb.PIPELINE_CONFIGS[opts.pipeline_config], fps,
                                    profile=tb.get_braking_profile(scenario))
        cam_x, cam_y = site.pole_xy
        started = time.monotonic()
        try:
            for index in range(n_frames):
                t = index * dt
                cast.drive_tick(t)
                for rig in rigs:
                    rig.move(session, t)
                if ambient is not None:
                    ambient.tick()
                frame_id = session.tick()
                data = hub.collect(frame_id)
                agents_now = scripted_agents(scenario, t)
                state = tb.run_pipeline_on_agents(pipeline, agents_now, t, cam_x=cam_x,
                                                  cam_y=cam_y)
                images: Dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
                aux: Dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
                cameras = {}
                for rig in rigs:
                    img, extra_aux = rig.frame(data, t)
                    images[rig.name] = img
                    aux.update(extra_aux)
                    cameras[rig.name] = rig.camera(t)
                frame = FrameRecord(
                    index=index, t=t,
                    agents=cast.states(t, {a["id"]: a for a in agents_now}),
                    state=state, states={opts.pipeline_config: state},
                    alert_pair=_alert_pair(pipeline, state), danger=danger_for(scenario, t),
                    cameras=cameras, images=images, aux=aux)
                recorder.write(frame)
            summary = recorder.close()
        except BaseException:
            try:
                recorder.close()
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                log.debug("recorder close after failure: %s", exc)
            raise
        finally:
            if ambient is not None:
                ambient.stop()
        summary["seconds"] = round(time.monotonic() - started, 1)
        summary["run"] = run.to_dict()
        return summary

docs.title: projection
docs.text:
Rotation conventions and camera projection for rendered views.

All world quantities are in the CARLA world frame (metres, left-handed, z up) and rotations are (pitch, yaw, roll) in degrees with the Unreal convention of carla.Rotation. A camera is a :class:~bikeped.sim.types.CameraModel; its camera coordinates are (f, r, u) along forward, right and up.

Pixel conventions follow the source of the intrinsics. Pinhole models use the CARLA convention, principal point at (width / 2, height / 2). Fisheye models use the calibration convention of camera_calibration.json and decision_testbench.FisheyeCamera, in which pixel centres sit at integer coordinates.

Return the world-frame (forward, right, up) unit vectors of a rotation.

Angles are in degrees. The result equals carla.Transform(rotation=...) .get_forward_vector(), .get_right_vector() and .get_up_vector().

def carla_rotation_to_basis(pitch: float, yaw: float, roll: float) -> Tuple[Vec, Vec, Vec]:
    """Return the world-frame ``(forward, right, up)`` unit vectors of a rotation.

    Angles are in degrees. The result equals ``carla.Transform(rotation=...)``
    ``.get_forward_vector()``, ``.get_right_vector()`` and ``.get_up_vector()``.
    """
    p, y, r = np.radians([pitch, yaw, roll])
    cp, sp = math.cos(p), math.sin(p)
    cy, sy = math.cos(y), math.sin(y)
    cr, sr = math.cos(r), math.sin(r)
    forward = (cp * cy, cp * sy, sp)
    right = (sr * sp * cy - cr * sy, sr * sp * sy + cr * cy, -sr * cp)
    up = (-(cr * sp * cy + sr * sy), cy * sr - cr * sp * sy, cr * cp)
    return forward, right, up

docs.text:
basis_to_carla_rotation(
    forward: Sequence[float], right: Sequence[float], up: Sequence[float]
) -> Tuple[float, float, float]

Return (pitch, yaw, roll) in degrees for an orthonormal camera basis.

Inverse of :func:carla_rotation_to_basis. At pitch of plus or minus 90 degrees only yaw + roll (or yaw - roll) is defined; roll is then set to zero and the whole in-plane rotation goes into yaw.

Source code in bikeped/sim/projection.py 
def basis_to_carla_rotation(forward: Sequence[float], right: Sequence[float],
                            up: Sequence[float]) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:
    """Return ``(pitch, yaw, roll)`` in degrees for an orthonormal camera basis.

    Inverse of :func:`carla_rotation_to_basis`. At pitch of plus or minus 90
    degrees only ``yaw + roll`` (or ``yaw - roll``) is defined; roll is then set
    to zero and the whole in-plane rotation goes into yaw.
    """
    f = np.asarray(forward, dtype=np.float64)
    r = np.asarray(right, dtype=np.float64)
    u = np.asarray(up, dtype=np.float64)
    pitch = math.degrees(math.asin(float(np.clip(f[2], -1.0, 1.0))))
    if math.hypot(f[0], f[1]) > 1e-9:
        yaw = math.degrees(math.atan2(f[1], f[0]))
        roll = math.degrees(math.atan2(-r[2], u[2]))
    else:
        # With roll = 0 the right vector is (-sin yaw, cos yaw, 0) at any pitch.
        yaw = math.degrees(math.atan2(-r[0], r[1]))
        roll = 0.0
    return pitch, yaw, roll

box_corners_world(
    location: Sequence[float], rotation: Sequence[float], extent: Sequence[float]
) -> np.ndarray

Return the 8 world-frame corners of an oriented box as an (8, 3) array.

location is the box centre, rotation (pitch, yaw, roll) in degrees, extent the half sizes along the box forward, right and up axes. Corner 4*ix + 2*iy + iz lies on the minus (0) or plus (1) side of each axis, so corners 0, 2, 6, 4 form the bottom face.

Source code in bikeped/sim/projection.py 
def box_corners_world(location: Sequence[float], rotation: Sequence[float],
                      extent: Sequence[float]) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return the 8 world-frame corners of an oriented box as an ``(8, 3)`` array.

    ``location`` is the box centre, ``rotation`` ``(pitch, yaw, roll)`` in
    degrees, ``extent`` the half sizes along the box forward, right and up axes.
    Corner ``4*ix + 2*iy + iz`` lies on the minus (0) or plus (1) side of each
    axis, so corners 0, 2, 6, 4 form the bottom face.
    """
    basis = np.array(carla_rotation_to_basis(*rotation), dtype=np.float64)
    ext = np.asarray(extent, dtype=np.float64)
    signs = np.array([[1 if i & 4 else -1, 1 if i & 2 else -1, 1 if i & 1 else -1]
                      for i in range(8)], dtype=np.float64)
    return np.asarray(location, dtype=np.float64) + (signs * ext) @ basis

def world_to_camera(points_w: np.ndarray, cam: CameraModel) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return camera coordinates ``(f, r, u)`` in metres of ``(N, 3)`` world points."""
    pts = np.asarray(points_w, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1, 3)
    return (pts - np.asarray(cam.position, dtype=np.float64)) @ cam.basis().T

def fisheye_focal(cam: CameraModel) -> float:
    """Equidistant focal length in pixels per radian of a fisheye model."""
    if cam.f_px_per_rad is not None:
        return float(cam.f_px_per_rad)
    if cam.circle_radius_px is None:
        raise ValueError(f"fisheye camera {cam.name!r} needs f_px_per_rad or circle_radius_px")
    return float(cam.circle_radius_px) / math.radians(cam.fov_deg / 2.0)

docs.text:
camera_to_image(
    fru: ndarray, cam: CameraModel
) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]

Project camera coordinates (N, 3) to pixels; see :func:project_points.

Source code in bikeped/sim/projection.py 
def camera_to_image(fru: np.ndarray, cam: CameraModel) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Project camera coordinates ``(N, 3)`` to pixels; see :func:`project_points`."""
    fru = np.asarray(fru, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1, 3)
    f, r, u = fru[:, 0], fru[:, 1], fru[:, 2]
    cx, cy = cam.principal_point
    if cam.kind == "pinhole":
        valid = f > NEAR_PLANE_M
        safe = np.where(valid, f, 1.0)
        fpx = cam.focal_px
        uv = np.stack([cx + fpx * r / safe, cy - fpx * u / safe], axis=1)
        return uv, valid, f.copy()
    if cam.kind == "fisheye":
        rng = np.linalg.norm(fru, axis=1)
        lateral = np.hypot(r, u)
        theta = np.arctan2(lateral, f)
        rad = _fisheye_radius(theta, cam)
        scale = np.where(lateral > 1e-12, rad / np.maximum(lateral, 1e-12), 0.0)
        uv = np.stack([cx + scale * r, cy - scale * u], axis=1)
        valid = (theta <= math.radians(cam.fov_deg / 2.0)) & (rng > 1e-9)
        return uv, valid, rng
    raise ValueError(f"unknown camera kind {cam.kind!r}")

For a fisheye a point is valid inside the field of view and depth is the Euclidean range. Validity does not test the image bounds.

def project_points(points_w: np.ndarray,
                   cam: CameraModel) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Project world points to pixels.

    Returns ``uv`` ``(N, 2)``, ``valid`` ``(N,)`` and ``depth`` ``(N,)``.
    For a pinhole camera a point is valid in front of the near plane and depth
    is the distance along the optical axis, as in a CARLA depth image. For a
    fisheye a point is valid inside the field of view and depth is the
    Euclidean range. Validity does not test the image bounds.
    """
    return camera_to_image(world_to_camera(points_w, cam), cam)

docs.text:
project_polyline(
    points_w: ndarray,
    cam: CameraModel,
    *,
    max_step_px: float = 6.0,
    closed: bool = False,
) -> List[np.ndarray]

Project a world polyline to a list of image polylines (M, 2), M >= 2.

Pinhole segments are clipped exactly at the near plane and stay straight. Fisheye segments are resampled so that consecutive samples are at most about max_step_px apart, since straight lines map to curves, and the polyline is split where it leaves the field of view.

Source code in bikeped/sim/projection.py 
def project_polyline(points_w: np.ndarray, cam: CameraModel, *, max_step_px: float = 6.0,
                     closed: bool = False) -> List[np.ndarray]:
    """Project a world polyline to a list of image polylines ``(M, 2)``, ``M >= 2``.

    Pinhole segments are clipped exactly at the near plane and stay straight.
    Fisheye segments are resampled so that consecutive samples are at most
    about ``max_step_px`` apart, since straight lines map to curves, and the
    polyline is split where it leaves the field of view.
    """
    pts = np.asarray(points_w, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1, 3)
    if closed and len(pts) > 2:
        pts = np.vstack([pts, pts[:1]])
    if len(pts) < 2:
        return []
    fru = world_to_camera(pts, cam)
    pieces: List[np.ndarray] = []
    current: List[np.ndarray] = []

    def flush() -> None:
        if len(current) >= 2:
            pieces.append(np.vstack(current))
        current.clear()

    for a, b in zip(fru[:-1], fru[1:]):
        if cam.kind == "pinhole":
            clipped = _clip_near(a, b)
            if clipped is None:
                flush()
                continue
            ca, cb = clipped
            uv, _, _ = camera_to_image(np.vstack([ca, cb]), cam)
            if current and ca is not a:
                flush()
            if not current:
                current.append(uv[:1])
            current.append(uv[1:])
            if cb is not b:
                flush()
        else:
            n = _segment_samples(a, b, cam, max_step_px)
            s = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, n + 1)[:, None]
            uv, valid, _ = camera_to_image(a + (b - a) * s, cam)
            start = 1 if current else 0
            for k in range(start, len(uv)):
                if valid[k]:
                    current.append(uv[k:k + 1])
                else:
                    flush()
    flush()
    return pieces

docs.text:
project_box(agent: AgentState, cam: CameraModel) -> Optional[Dict[str, object]]

Project an agent's oriented 3D box into a view.

Returns None when no part of the box is in front of the camera or inside the image. Otherwise a dict with bbox [x1, y1, x2, y2] clipped to the image, corners_image (8, 2) with NaN rows for corners behind the near plane or outside the field of view, truncation (fraction of the unclipped box area outside the image) and distance_m (camera to box centre). Pinhole edges are clipped against the near plane one by one, so a box that straddles the camera keeps its true extent; fisheye edges are sampled densely because they curve.

Source code in bikeped/sim/projection.py 
def project_box(agent: AgentState, cam: CameraModel) -> Optional[Dict[str, object]]:
    """Project an agent's oriented 3D box into a view.

    Returns ``None`` when no part of the box is in front of the camera or
    inside the image. Otherwise a dict with ``bbox`` ``[x1, y1, x2, y2]``
    clipped to the image, ``corners_image`` ``(8, 2)`` with NaN rows for
    corners behind the near plane or outside the field of view,
    ``truncation`` (fraction of the unclipped box area outside the image) and
    ``distance_m`` (camera to box centre). Pinhole edges are clipped against
    the near plane one by one, so a box that straddles the camera keeps its
    true extent; fisheye edges are sampled densely because they curve.
    """
    corners = box_corners_world(agent.location, agent.rotation, agent.extent)
    uv, valid, _ = project_points(corners, cam)
    corners_image = np.where(valid[:, None], uv, np.nan)
    samples: List[np.ndarray] = []
    for i, j in BOX_EDGES:
        for piece in project_polyline(corners[[i, j]], cam, max_step_px=4.0):
            samples.append(piece)
    if not samples:
        return None
    allpts = np.vstack(samples)
    x1, y1 = allpts.min(axis=0)
    x2, y2 = allpts.max(axis=0)
    cx1, cy1 = max(x1, 0.0), max(y1, 0.0)
    cx2, cy2 = min(x2, float(cam.width)), min(y2, float(cam.height))
    if cx2 <= cx1 or cy2 <= cy1:
        return None
    full = max((x2 - x1) * (y2 - y1), 1e-12)
    inside = (cx2 - cx1) * (cy2 - cy1)
    distance = float(np.linalg.norm(np.asarray(agent.location) - np.asarray(cam.position)))
    return {
        "bbox": [float(cx1), float(cy1), float(cx2), float(cy2)],
        "corners_image": corners_image,
        "truncation": float(np.clip(1.0 - inside / full, 0.0, 1.0)),
        "distance_m": distance,
    }

docs.text:
pixel_rays(uv: ndarray, cam: CameraModel) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]

Return world-frame unit ray directions (N, 3) and a validity mask for pixels.

Source code in bikeped/sim/projection.py 
def pixel_rays(uv: np.ndarray, cam: CameraModel) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Return world-frame unit ray directions ``(N, 3)`` and a validity mask for pixels."""
    pix = np.asarray(uv, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1, 2)
    cx, cy = cam.principal_point
    du, dv = pix[:, 0] - cx, pix[:, 1] - cy
    if cam.kind == "pinhole":
        fpx = cam.focal_px
        fru = np.stack([np.ones(len(pix)), du / fpx, -dv / fpx], axis=1)
        valid = np.ones(len(pix), dtype=bool)
    elif cam.kind == "fisheye":
        rad = np.hypot(du, dv)
        theta = _fisheye_theta(rad, cam)
        phi = np.arctan2(dv, du)
        st = np.sin(theta)
        fru = np.stack([np.cos(theta), st * np.cos(phi), -st * np.sin(phi)], axis=1)
        valid = theta <= math.radians(cam.fov_deg / 2.0)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown camera kind {cam.kind!r}")
    rays = fru @ cam.basis()
    rays /= np.linalg.norm(rays, axis=1, keepdims=True)
    return rays, valid

    uv: ndarray, cam: CameraModel, ground_z: float = 0.0
) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]

Intersect pixel rays with the horizontal plane z = ground_z.

Returns world points (N, 3) (NaN where invalid) and valid (N,), false for rays outside the field of view or not pointing at the plane.

def pixel_to_ground(uv: np.ndarray, cam: CameraModel,
                    ground_z: float = 0.0) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Intersect pixel rays with the horizontal plane ``z = ground_z``.

    Returns world points ``(N, 3)`` (NaN where invalid) and ``valid`` ``(N,)``,
    false for rays outside the field of view or not pointing at the plane.
    """
    rays, valid = pixel_rays(uv, cam)
    pos = np.asarray(cam.position, dtype=np.float64)
    rz = rays[:, 2]
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        t = (ground_z - pos[2]) / rz
    valid = valid & (np.abs(rz) > 1e-9) & (t > 0)
    pts = pos + rays * np.where(valid, t, 0.0)[:, None]
    pts[~valid] = np.nan
    return pts, valid

docs.title: fisheye
docs.text:
The deployed fisheye lens as a sim camera, and cube-face to fisheye remapping.

CARLA has no equidistant fisheye sensor, so the fisheye view is rendered as a set of 90 degree pinhole cameras sharing one position (the faces of a cube around the fisheye's optical axis) and resampled into the fisheye image with a lookup table built once by :class:FisheyeRemap.

:func:deployed_fisheye_model reproduces the lens of the field deployment. The calibration describes a 3500 x 3500 frame centred on the image circle; the physical sensor is 3840 x 2160, which is that frame padded to 3840 x 3840 and cropped to the middle 2160 rows, so the top and bottom of the circle are cut (rows 670 to 2829 of the 3500 px frame are on the sensor). The sim camera renders the sensor image, so its principal point is the calibrated one shifted by (+170, -670) pixels. With the same pose it agrees with decision_testbench.FisheyeCamera.world_to_pixel after that shift.

docs.title: FisheyeRemap
docs.text:
FisheyeRemap(
    model: CameraModel,
    face_size: int = 1024,
    supersample: int = 1,
    interpolation: int = cv2.INTER_LINEAR,
    feather_px: float = 1.5,
)

Lookup table from cube-face pinhole images to a fisheye image.

Every face is a square face_size pinhole camera with a 90 degree field of view at the fisheye position. Faces are oriented relative to the fisheye's optical axis (front, right, back, left, up, down); :attr:faces lists only those that receive pixels inside the image circle and on the sensor. supersample renders the lookup at an integer multiple of the output resolution and averages down, which anti-aliases fine texture near the rim of the circle.

Source code in bikeped/sim/fisheye.py 
def __init__(self, model: CameraModel, face_size: int = 1024, supersample: int = 1,
             interpolation: int = cv2.INTER_LINEAR, feather_px: float = 1.5) -> None:
    if model.kind != "fisheye":
        raise ValueError("FisheyeRemap needs a fisheye CameraModel")
    self.model = model
    self.face_size = int(face_size)
    self.supersample = max(1, int(supersample))
    self.interpolation = interpolation
    gx, gy = _output_grid(model, self.supersample)
    shape = gx.shape
    rays, valid = pixel_rays(np.stack([gx.ravel(), gy.ravel()], axis=1), model)
    fru = rays @ model.basis().T
    signed = np.concatenate([fru, -fru], axis=1)
    choice = np.argmax(signed, axis=1)
    names = {(0, 1): "front", (1, 1): "right", (2, 1): "up",
             (0, -1): "back", (1, -1): "left", (2, -1): "down"}
    self._lookup: Dict[str, Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]] = {}
    half = self.face_size / 2.0
    for k in range(6):
        face = names[(k % 3, 1 if k < 3 else -1)]
        idx = np.flatnonzero(valid & (choice == k))
        if idx.size == 0:
            continue
        axes = _FACE_AXES[face]
        comp = [fru[idx, a] * s for a, s in axes]
        f = np.maximum(comp[0], 1e-9)
        # Face cameras follow the CARLA pinhole convention: principal point
        # at the image centre and pixel i covering [i, i + 1).
        mx = half + half * comp[1] / f - 0.5
        my = half - half * comp[2] / f - 0.5
        self._lookup[face] = (idx, _as_map(mx), _as_map(my))
    order = ("down", "front", "right", "back", "left", "up")
    self.faces: Tuple[str, ...] = tuple(f for f in order if f in self._lookup)
    self._shape = shape
    cx, cy = model.principal_point
    ox, oy = _output_grid(model, 1)
    radius = np.hypot(ox - cx, oy - cy)
    edge = float(model.circle_radius_px) if model.circle_radius_px else float(radius.max())
    feather = max(float(feather_px), 1e-3)
    self.mask = np.clip((edge - radius) / feather + 0.5, 0.0, 1.0).astype(np.float32)

def face_camera(self, face: str) -> CameraModel:
    """Return the 90 degree square pinhole :class:`CameraModel` of a cube face.

    Its basis converts to a CARLA rotation with
    :func:`~bikeped.sim.projection.basis_to_carla_rotation`.
    """
    if face not in _FACE_AXES:
        raise KeyError(f"unknown face {face!r}")
    b = self.model.basis()
    f, r, u = (b[a] * s for a, s in _FACE_AXES[face])
    return CameraModel(name=f"{self.model.name}/{face}", kind="pinhole",
                       width=self.face_size, height=self.face_size,
                       position=self.model.position, forward=tuple(f), right=tuple(r),
                       up=tuple(u), fov_deg=90.0)

remap(face_images: Dict[str, ndarray]) -> np.ndarray

Resample BGR face images into the fisheye image (uint8, black outside the circle).

face_images must hold every face in :attr:faces. Images of a different size than face_size are accepted and sampled in proportion.

Source code in bikeped/sim/fisheye.py 
def remap(self, face_images: Dict[str, np.ndarray]) -> np.ndarray:
    """Resample BGR face images into the fisheye image (``uint8``, black outside the circle).

    ``face_images`` must hold every face in :attr:`faces`. Images of a
    different size than ``face_size`` are accepted and sampled in proportion.
    """
    h, w = self._shape
    out = np.zeros((h * w, 3), dtype=np.float32)
    for face in self.faces:
        if face not in face_images:
            raise KeyError(f"missing face image {face!r}; need {self.faces}")
        img = np.asarray(face_images[face])
        if img.ndim == 2:
            img = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_GRAY2BGR)
        img = img[..., :3]
        idx, mx, my = self._lookup[face]
        sx, sy = img.shape[1] / self.face_size, img.shape[0] / self.face_size
        if sx != 1.0 or sy != 1.0:
            mx = ((mx + 0.5) * sx - 0.5).astype(np.float32)
            my = ((my + 0.5) * sy - 0.5).astype(np.float32)
        sampled = cv2.remap(img, mx, my, self.interpolation, borderMode=cv2.BORDER_REPLICATE)
        out[idx] = sampled.reshape(-1, 3)[:idx.size]
    out = out.reshape(h, w, 3)
    if self.supersample > 1:
        out = cv2.resize(out, (self.model.width, self.model.height),
                         interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)
    out *= self.mask[..., None]
    return np.clip(out + 0.5, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)

    counter-clockwise from ``+x``) is CARLA yaw ``-h`` once the scenario
    ``y`` axis is flipped into the left-handed world, so the testbench default
    (heading 90 degrees) is ``yaw_deg=-90``.
    """
    p = _load_camera_parameters(calibration, config)
    pitch = p["pitch_deg"] if pitch_deg is None else float(pitch_deg)
    forward, right, up = carla_rotation_to_basis(pitch, yaw_deg, 0.0)
    x_off = (PAD_SIZE - CROP_SIZE) // 2
    y_off = (PAD_SIZE - CROP_SIZE) // 2 - (PAD_SIZE - SENSOR_SIZE[1]) // 2
    width = max(2, int(round(SENSOR_SIZE[0] * scale / 2.0)) * 2)
    height = max(2, int(round(SENSOR_SIZE[1] * scale / 2.0)) * 2)
    sx, sy = width / SENSOR_SIZE[0], height / SENSOR_SIZE[1]
    # Pixel centres sit at integer coordinates, so scaling acts on (x + 0.5).
    cx = (p["cx"] + x_off + 0.5) * sx - 0.5
    cy = (p["cy"] + y_off + 0.5) * sy - 0.5
    radius = p["radius_px"] * sx
    return CameraModel(
        name=name, kind="fisheye", width=width, height=height,
        position=tuple(float(v) for v in position), forward=forward, right=right, up=up,
        fov_deg=p["fov_deg"], cx=cx, cy=cy,
        f_px_per_rad=radius / math.radians(p["fov_deg"] / 2.0),
        k1=p["k1"], k2=p["k2"], circle_radius_px=radius,
    )

synthetic_faces(
    remap: FisheyeRemap,
    pattern: str = "grid",
    *,
    ground_z: float = 0.0,
    cell_m: float = 1.0,
    markers: Sequence[Sequence[float]] = (),
) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]

Render face images of an analytic scene, for tests and demos.

The scene is the plane z = ground_z (world metres) painted as a checkerboard (pattern='checker') or a light grid on asphalt grey (pattern='grid') with cell_m cells, under a vertical sky gradient. Each entry of markers is a world (x, y) drawn as a pure red (BGR (0, 0, 255)) disc of 0.15 m radius.

Source code in bikeped/sim/fisheye.py 
def synthetic_faces(remap: FisheyeRemap, pattern: str = "grid", *, ground_z: float = 0.0,
                    cell_m: float = 1.0,
                    markers: Sequence[Sequence[float]] = ()) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    """Render face images of an analytic scene, for tests and demos.

    The scene is the plane ``z = ground_z`` (world metres) painted as a
    checkerboard (``pattern='checker'``) or a light grid on asphalt grey
    (``pattern='grid'``) with ``cell_m`` cells, under a vertical sky gradient.
    Each entry of ``markers`` is a world ``(x, y)`` drawn as a pure red
    (BGR ``(0, 0, 255)``) disc of 0.15 m radius.
    """
    if pattern not in ("grid", "checker"):
        raise ValueError(f"unknown pattern {pattern!r}")
    images: Dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
    n = remap.face_size
    xs = np.arange(n, dtype=np.float64) + 0.5
    gu, gv = np.meshgrid(xs, xs)
    uv = np.stack([gu.ravel(), gv.ravel()], axis=1)
    pos = np.asarray(remap.model.position, dtype=np.float64)
    for face in remap.faces:
        cam = remap.face_camera(face)
        rays, _ = pixel_rays(uv, cam)
        elev = np.clip(rays[:, 2], -1.0, 1.0)
        sky = np.stack([235 - 60 * elev, 205 - 70 * elev, 170 - 90 * elev], axis=1)
        img = np.clip(sky, 0, 255)
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            t = (ground_z - pos[2]) / rays[:, 2]
        hit = np.isfinite(t) & (t > 0)
        gx = pos[0] + rays[:, 0] * np.where(hit, t, 0.0)
        gy = pos[1] + rays[:, 1] * np.where(hit, t, 0.0)
        if pattern == "checker":
            parity = (np.floor(gx / cell_m) + np.floor(gy / cell_m)) % 2
            ground = np.where(parity[:, None] > 0, [[200, 200, 200]], [[60, 60, 60]])
        else:
            fx = np.abs(gx / cell_m - np.round(gx / cell_m))
            fy = np.abs(gy / cell_m - np.round(gy / cell_m))
            line = np.minimum(fx, fy) * cell_m < 0.03
            ground = np.where(line[:, None], [[215, 215, 210]], [[78, 76, 74]])
        for mx_, my_ in markers:
            disc = np.hypot(gx - mx_, gy - my_) < 0.15
            ground = np.where(disc[:, None], [[0, 0, 255]], ground)
        img = np.where(hit[:, None], ground, img)
        images[face] = img.reshape(n, n, 3).astype(np.uint8)
    return images

def danger_record(scenario: Mapping[str, Any], t: float) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Ground-truth danger at time ``t`` (seconds) as a JSON-safe dict.

    Wraps ``decision_testbench.compute_ground_truth_danger``; the keys are the
    fields of its ``DangerAssessment`` (distances in metres, speeds in m/s,
    times in seconds) and infinite values become ``None``.
    """
    assessment = _testbench().compute_ground_truth_danger(dict(scenario), float(t))
    return {k: _json_number(v) for k, v in asdict(assessment).items()}

docs.text:
closest_pair(frame: FrameRecord) -> Optional[Tuple[int, int, float]]

Nearest scripted (bike_id, person_id, distance_m) in the scenario frame, or None.

Source code in bikeped/sim/groundtruth.py 
def closest_pair(frame: FrameRecord) -> Optional[Tuple[int, int, float]]:
    """Nearest scripted ``(bike_id, person_id, distance_m)`` in the scenario frame, or ``None``."""
    bikes = [a for a in frame.agents if a.role == "scripted" and a.kind == "bike"]
    people = [a for a in frame.agents if a.role == "scripted" and a.kind == "person"]
    best: Optional[Tuple[int, int, float]] = None
    for b in bikes:
        for p in people:
            d = math.hypot(b.sx - p.sx, b.sy - p.sy)
            if best is None or d < best[2]:
                best = (b.id, p.id, d)
    return best

synthetic_agents(
    scenario: Mapping[str, Any], t: float, ground_z: float = 0.0
) -> List[AgentState]

Scripted agents at time t with testbench box sizes.

Positions are placed with :func:scenario_to_world; speeds are in m/s.

def synthetic_agents(scenario: Mapping[str, Any], t: float,
                     ground_z: float = 0.0) -> List[AgentState]:
    """Scripted agents at time ``t`` with testbench box sizes.

    Positions are placed with :func:`scenario_to_world`; speeds are in m/s.
    """
    tb = _testbench()
    agents: List[AgentState] = []
    for agent_def in scenario["agents"]:
        pose = tb.interpolate_agent(agent_def, t)
        if pose is None:
            continue
        obj = tb.OBJECT_TYPES[KIND_TO_OBJECT.get(agent_def["type"], "pedestrian")]
        agents.append(AgentState(
            id=int(agent_def["id"]), kind=agent_def["type"], sx=float(pose["x"]),
            sy=float(pose["y"]), heading=float(pose["heading"]),
            speed=float(tb.estimate_agent_speed(agent_def, t)),
            location=scenario_to_world(pose["x"], pose["y"], ground_z + obj.height / 2.0),
            rotation=(0.0, -math.degrees(pose["heading"]), 0.0),
            extent=(obj.length / 2.0, obj.width / 2.0, obj.height / 2.0),
            model=str(agent_def.get("model", "")),
        ))
    return agents

def synthetic_frame(scenario: Mapping[str, Any], index: int, fps: int,
                    cameras: Optional[Dict[str, CameraModel]] = None,
                    states: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> FrameRecord:
    """A :class:`FrameRecord` at ``t = index / fps`` built from the scenario alone, without images.

    ``state`` is ``states[index]`` when given, else ``"idle"``; in the alert
    state ``alert_pair`` is the closest bike and pedestrian.
    """
    t = index / float(fps)
    state = states[index] if states is not None and index < len(states) else "idle"
    frame = FrameRecord(index=index, t=t, agents=synthetic_agents(scenario, t), state=state,
                        states={"default": state}, danger=danger_record(scenario, t),
                        cameras=dict(cameras or {}))
    if state == "alert":
        pair = closest_pair(frame)
        if pair is not None:
            frame.alert_pair = (pair[0], pair[1])
    return frame

frame_ground_truth(frame: FrameRecord, view: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]

Per-agent ground truth of one view, JSON-safe.

Each entry has id, kind, role, bbox (pixels, clipped to the image), corners_image (8 [u, v] or None), distance_m, truncation and visible_fraction. The visible fraction is the share of the agent's projected silhouette carrying its id in aux['<view>/instance'] when that buffer and AgentState.instance_id exist, else the share of camera-facing box surface samples not occluded in aux['<view>/depth'] (planar depth for pinhole views, range for fisheye views), else None. Agents outside the view are omitted.

Source code in bikeped/sim/groundtruth.py 
def frame_ground_truth(frame: FrameRecord, view: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Per-agent ground truth of one view, JSON-safe.

    Each entry has ``id``, ``kind``, ``role``, ``bbox`` (pixels, clipped to
    the image), ``corners_image`` (8 ``[u, v]`` or ``None``), ``distance_m``,
    ``truncation`` and ``visible_fraction``. The visible fraction is the share
    of the agent's projected silhouette carrying its id in
    ``aux['<view>/instance']`` when that buffer and ``AgentState.instance_id``
    exist, else the share of camera-facing box surface samples not occluded in
    ``aux['<view>/depth']`` (planar depth for pinhole views, range for
    fisheye views), else ``None``. Agents outside the view are omitted.
    """
    from .projection import project_box

    cam = frame.cameras.get(view)
    if cam is None:
        return []
    depth = frame.aux.get(f"{view}/depth")
    instance = frame.aux.get(f"{view}/instance")
    objects: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    for agent in frame.agents:
        box = project_box(agent, cam)
        if box is None:
            continue
        visible: Optional[float] = None
        if instance is not None:
            visible = _visible_from_instance(agent, cam, instance)
        if visible is None and depth is not None:
            visible = _visible_from_depth(agent, cam, depth)
        corners = [None if not np.all(np.isfinite(c)) else [round(float(c[0]), 2),
                                                             round(float(c[1]), 2)]
                   for c in box["corners_image"]]
        objects.append({
            "id": agent.id, "kind": agent.kind, "role": agent.role,
            "bbox": [round(float(v), 2) for v in box["bbox"]],
            "corners_image": corners,
            "distance_m": round(float(box["distance_m"]), 3),
            "truncation": round(float(box["truncation"]), 4),
            "visible_fraction": None if visible is None else round(visible, 4),
        })
    return objects

HUD overlay and schematic top-down panel for rendered scenario frames.

draw_overlay annotates one camera view with 3D boxes, id chips, ground trails, the bike-pedestrian connector, the decision state badge and a timeline of ground-truth danger against the system's alerts. draw_bev renders the same frame as a plan view in the scenario frame. build_timeline(
    scenario: Dict[str, Any], fps: int, states: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None
) -> Dict[str, Any]

Precompute what the timeline strip shows for one scenario.

Frame i is at t = i / fps. Ground-truth danger comes from decision_testbench.compute_ground_truth_danger. states is the decision state per frame as recorded by a run; when it is None the states come from decision_testbench.simulate_scenario with the default pipeline configuration and no detection noise, and the result is cached per scenario and frame rate.

Returns a dict with duration (s), fps, n (frames), states, the interval lists danger, actionable, alert and warning ([t0, t1] pairs in seconds, t1 exclusive), and first_alert_t and first_danger_t (seconds or None).

Source code in bikeped/sim/overlay.py 
def build_timeline(scenario: Dict[str, Any], fps: int,
                   states: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Precompute what the timeline strip shows for one scenario.

    Frame ``i`` is at ``t = i / fps``. Ground-truth danger comes from
    ``decision_testbench.compute_ground_truth_danger``. ``states`` is the
    decision state per frame as recorded by a run; when it is ``None`` the
    states come from ``decision_testbench.simulate_scenario`` with the default
    pipeline configuration and no detection noise, and the result is cached
    per scenario and frame rate.

    Returns a dict with ``duration`` (s), ``fps``, ``n`` (frames), ``states``,
    the interval lists ``danger``, ``actionable``, ``alert`` and ``warning``
    (``[t0, t1]`` pairs in seconds, ``t1`` exclusive), and ``first_alert_t``
    and ``first_danger_t`` (seconds or ``None``).
    """
    tb = _testbench()
    fps = int(fps)
    key = (_scenario_key(scenario), fps)
    if states is None and key in _TIMELINES:
        return _TIMELINES[key]
    dt = 1.0 / fps
    duration = float(tb.get_scenario_duration(scenario))
    if states is None:
        result = tb.simulate_scenario(scenario, tb.PIPELINE_CONFIGS["default"], fps=fps)
        state_list = [str(s) for s in result["states"]]
        danger = [bool(d) for d in result["dangers"]]
        actionable = [bool(a.actionable) for a in result["assessments"]]
        _DANGER[(key[0], fps, len(state_list))] = (danger, actionable)
    else:
        state_list = [str(s) for s in states]
        cached = _DANGER.get((key[0], fps, len(state_list)))
        if cached is None:
            assessments = [tb.compute_ground_truth_danger(scenario, i * dt)
                           for i in range(len(state_list))]
            cached = ([bool(a.is_danger) for a in assessments],
                      [bool(a.actionable) for a in assessments])
            _DANGER[(key[0], fps, len(state_list))] = cached
        danger, actionable = cached
    n = len(state_list)
    alert = [s == "alert" for s in state_list]
    timeline = {
        "duration": max(duration, n * dt),
        "fps": fps,
        "n": n,
        "states": state_list,
        "danger": _intervals(danger, dt),
        "actionable": _intervals(actionable, dt),
        "alert": _intervals(alert, dt),
        "warning": _intervals([s == "warning" for s in state_list], dt),
        "first_alert_t": round(alert.index(True) * dt, 4) if any(alert) else None,
        "first_danger_t": round(danger.index(True) * dt, 4) if any(danger) else None,
    }
    if states is None:
        _TIMELINES[key] = timeline
    return timeline

Source code in bikeped/sim/overlay.py 
def draw_overlay(image: np.ndarray, frame: FrameRecord, view: str, *, run: RunInfo,
                 scenario: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
                 style: Optional[OverlayStyle] = None,
                 history: Optional[Sequence[FrameRecord]] = None,
                 timeline: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> np.ndarray:
    """Draw the HUD over one rendered view and return the annotated copy.

    ``image`` is the BGR ``uint8`` frame of ``view`` and is not modified. The
    camera model is ``frame.cameras[view]``; without one only the screen-space
    elements (badge, caption, timeline) are drawn. ``history`` holds earlier
    frames, oldest first, and feeds the ground trails from the bottom centre of
    each agent's box in the world frame. ``timeline`` is the result of
    ``build_timeline``; when it is ``None`` and ``scenario`` is given it is
    built from the scenario at ``run.fps``.
    """
    style = style or DEFAULT_STYLE
    out = np.ascontiguousarray(image).copy()
    if out.ndim == 2:
        out = cv2.cvtColor(out, cv2.COLOR_GRAY2BGR)
    canvas = _Canvas(out, style)
    cam = frame.cameras.get(view)
    if timeline is None and scenario is not None and style.timeline:
        timeline = build_timeline(scenario, run.fps)
    show_timeline = style.timeline and timeline is not None

    margin = canvas.px(28)
    lanes_h = 2 * canvas.px(6, 3) + canvas.px(5, 2)
    timeline_y = canvas.h - margin - lanes_h
    caption_font = canvas.px(16, 9)
    caption_h = canvas.text_size("Ag", caption_font)[1]
    caption_y = (timeline_y - canvas.px(14) - caption_h) if show_timeline else (
        canvas.h - margin - caption_h)
    hud_top = caption_y if style.caption else (timeline_y if show_timeline else canvas.h)
    if style.caption or show_timeline:
        canvas.scrim(int(hud_top - canvas.px(70)), canvas.h, 0.0, 0.66)

    occupied: List[Rect] = []
    if style.caption or show_timeline:
        occupied.append((0.0, hud_top - canvas.px(6), float(canvas.w), float(canvas.h)))
    badge_h = canvas.px(42, 20)
    if style.badge:
        occupied.append((0.0, 0.0, margin + canvas.px(250), margin + badge_h + canvas.px(40)))

    scripted = [a for a in frame.agents if a.role == "scripted"]
    if cam is not None:
        ground_z = run.site.get("ground_z")
        if ground_z is None:
            ground_z = min((_bottom_center(a)[2] for a in frame.agents), default=0.0)
        if style.rings or view in style.ring_views:
            boxes = [project_box(a, cam) for a in frame.agents]
            _draw_rings(canvas, cam, float(ground_z), occupied,
                        [tuple(b["bbox"]) for b in boxes if b is not None])
        if style.trails and history:
            _draw_trails(canvas, frame, cam, history)

        pair = _pair(frame) if style.connector else None
        highlighted = set()
        if pair is not None and pair[2] <= style.connector_max_m:
            a, b, distance = pair
            color = _connector_color(style, frame.state)
            if frame.state in ("alert", "warning"):
                highlighted = {a.id, b.id}
            ends = np.stack([_bottom_center(a), _bottom_center(b)])
            pieces = project_polyline(ends, cam)
            canvas.lines(pieces, style.bgr("background"), canvas.px(5), alpha=0.45)
            canvas.lines(pieces, color, canvas.px(2))
            uv, valid, _ = project_points(ends.mean(axis=0, keepdims=True), cam)
            if valid[0] and 0 <= uv[0, 0] < canvas.w and 0 <= uv[0, 1] < canvas.h:
                label = f"{distance:.1f} m"
                font = canvas.px(15, 9)
                tw, th = canvas.text_size(label, font, bold=True)
                pad = canvas.px(9)
                rect = (uv[0, 0] - tw / 2.0 - pad, uv[0, 1] - th / 2.0 - canvas.px(4),
                        uv[0, 0] + tw / 2.0 + pad, uv[0, 1] + th / 2.0 + canvas.px(4))
                canvas.plate(rect, style.bgr("background"), alpha=0.86)
                canvas.text_centered(rect, label, font, color, bold=True)
                occupied.append(rect)

        cam_pos = np.asarray(cam.position, dtype=np.float64)
        ordered = sorted(frame.agents, reverse=True,
                         key=lambda ag: float(np.linalg.norm(np.asarray(ag.location) - cam_pos)))
        chips: List[Tuple[AgentState, Sequence[float]]] = []
        for agent in ordered:
            color = style.agent_color(agent.kind, agent.role)
            hot = agent.id in highlighted and agent.role == "scripted"
            if style.boxes:
                _draw_box(canvas, agent, cam, color,
                          style.state_color(frame.state) if hot else color, 0.34 if hot else 0.2)
            if style.labels and agent.role == "scripted":
                box = project_box(agent, cam)
                if box is not None:
                    chips.append((agent, box["bbox"]))
        font = canvas.px(14, 9)
        for agent, bbox in reversed(chips):
            text = _chip_text(agent)
            tw, _ = canvas.text_size(text, font, bold=True)
            size = (tw + 2 * canvas.px(8), canvas.px(22, 13))
            rect = _place_chip(canvas, size, bbox, occupied)
            occupied.append(rect)
            color = style.agent_color(agent.kind)
            anchor = ((bbox[0] + bbox[2]) / 2.0, bbox[1])
            foot = ((rect[0] + rect[2]) / 2.0, rect[3])
            if math.hypot(anchor[0] - foot[0], anchor[1] - foot[1]) > canvas.px(10):
                canvas.lines([np.array([foot, anchor])], color, canvas.px(1.25), alpha=0.6)
            outline = style.state_color(frame.state) if agent.id in highlighted else None
            _draw_chip(canvas, rect, text, color, outline)

    if style.badge:
        canvas.scrim(0, margin + badge_h + canvas.px(50), 0.3, 0.0)
        badge = _draw_badge(canvas, margin, margin, frame.state)
        danger = frame.danger or {}
        if danger.get("is_danger"):
            sep = " \u00b7 " if canvas.fonts.truetype else " | "
            note = "Ground truth: danger"
            if danger.get("ttc") is not None and math.isfinite(float(danger["ttc"])):
                note += f"{sep}TTC {float(danger['ttc']):.1f} s"
            font = canvas.px(13, 9)
            tw, th = canvas.text_size(note, font)
            pad = canvas.px(12)
            top = badge[3] + canvas.px(8)
            rect = (margin, top, margin + tw + 2 * pad, top + th + canvas.px(10))
            canvas.plate(rect, style.bgr("background"), alpha=0.7)
            canvas.text_centered(rect, note, font, style.bgr("alert"))

    if style.caption:
        sep = "  \u00b7  " if canvas.fonts.truetype else "  |  "
        title, details = _caption_parts(frame, run, sep)
        tw, _ = canvas.text(margin, caption_y, title, caption_font, style.bgr("text"), bold=True)
        if details:
            canvas.text(margin + tw, caption_y, sep + details, caption_font, style.bgr("muted"))
        total = timeline["duration"] if timeline else run.duration_s
        clock = f"{frame.t:5.2f} s" + (f" / {total:.2f} s" if total else "")
        cw, _ = canvas.text_size(clock, caption_font)
        canvas.text(canvas.w - margin - cw, caption_y, clock, caption_font, style.bgr("text"))
        tag = view.upper()
        vw, _ = canvas.text_size(tag, canvas.px(12, 8), bold=True)
        canvas.text(canvas.w - margin - cw - canvas.px(18) - vw,
                    caption_y + (caption_h - canvas.text_size(tag, canvas.px(12, 8), True)[1]) / 2,
                    tag, canvas.px(12, 8), style.bgr("muted"), bold=True)
    if show_timeline:
        _draw_timeline(canvas, timeline, frame.t, margin, canvas.w - margin, timeline_y)
    if scripted and cam is None:
        _LOG.debug("view %s has no camera model; drew screen-space HUD only", view)
    return out

Render the frame as a schematic plan view in the scenario frame.

size is (width, height) in pixels. The panel shows the road, the crosswalk at x = 5, the camera marker at run.site['camera_xy'] (the testbench camera position when absent) with the proximity rings of the default pipeline, the scripted paths, and every agent as an oriented glyph with a short trail. Scenario x points right and y up. Trails come from the scenario paths when scenario is given and from history otherwise. timeline adds the timeline strip at the bottom.

def draw_bev(frame: FrameRecord, *, run: RunInfo, scenario: Optional[Dict[str, Any]],
             size: Tuple[int, int] = (1080, 1080), style: Optional[OverlayStyle] = None,
             history: Optional[Sequence[FrameRecord]] = None,
             timeline: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> np.ndarray:
    """Render the frame as a schematic plan view in the scenario frame.

    ``size`` is ``(width, height)`` in pixels. The panel shows the road, the
    crosswalk at ``x = 5``, the camera marker at ``run.site['camera_xy']``
    (the testbench camera position when absent) with the proximity rings of
    the default pipeline, the scripted paths, and every agent as an oriented
    glyph with a short trail. Scenario ``x`` points right and ``y`` up. Trails
    come from the scenario paths when ``scenario`` is given and from
    ``history`` otherwise. ``timeline`` adds the timeline strip at the bottom.
    """
    style = style or DEFAULT_STYLE
    width, height = int(size[0]), int(size[1])
    cam_xy = _camera_xy(run)
    window = _bev_window(scenario, frame, cam_xy)
    key = (width, height, style, _scenario_key(scenario) if scenario else None,
           tuple(round(v, 3) for v in window), cam_xy)
    static = _BEV_STATIC.get(key)
    if static is None:
        static = _BEV_STATIC[key] = _bev_static((width, height), style, scenario, window, cam_xy)
        if len(_BEV_STATIC) > 8:
            _BEV_STATIC.popitem(last=False)
    out = static.copy()
    canvas = _Canvas(out, style)
    canvas.s = style.scale * min(width, height) / 1080.0
    to_px = _bev_mapper((width, height), window)
    metre = float(to_px([[1.0, 0.0]])[0][0] - to_px([[0.0, 0.0]])[0][0])
    bg = style.bgr("background")

    pair = _pair(frame) if style.connector else None
    highlighted = set()
    if pair is not None and pair[2] <= style.connector_max_m:
        a, b, distance = pair
        color = _connector_color(style, frame.state)
        if frame.state in ("alert", "warning"):
            highlighted = {a.id, b.id}
        ends = to_px([[a.sx, a.sy], [b.sx, b.sy]])
        canvas.lines([ends], color, canvas.px(2), alpha=0.9)
        mid = ends.mean(axis=0)
        label = f"{distance:.1f} m"
        font = canvas.px(15, 9)
        tw, th = canvas.text_size(label, font, bold=True)
        normal = np.array([-(ends[1][1] - ends[0][1]), ends[1][0] - ends[0][0]])
        length = float(np.linalg.norm(normal))
        if length > 1e-6:
            normal = normal / length
            if normal[1] > 0:
                normal = -normal
            mid = mid + normal * (th / 2.0 + canvas.px(12))
        rect = (mid[0] - tw / 2.0 - canvas.px(9), mid[1] - th / 2.0 - canvas.px(4),
                mid[0] + tw / 2.0 + canvas.px(9), mid[1] + th / 2.0 + canvas.px(4))
        canvas.plate(rect, bg, alpha=0.9)
        canvas.text_centered(rect, label, font, color, bold=True)

    for agent in frame.agents:
        color = style.agent_color(agent.kind, agent.role)
        if style.trails and agent.role == "scripted":
            trail = to_px(_bev_trail(frame, agent, scenario, history, style.trail_seconds))
            edges = np.linspace(0, len(trail) - 1, 6).round().astype(int)
            for band in range(5):
                chunk = trail[edges[band]:edges[band + 1] + 1]
                canvas.lines([chunk], color, canvas.px(4), alpha=0.18 + 0.62 * (band + 1) / 5)

    font = canvas.px(14, 9)
    for agent in frame.agents:
        color = style.agent_color(agent.kind, agent.role)
        center = to_px([[agent.sx, agent.sy]])[0]
        direction = np.array([math.cos(agent.heading), -math.sin(agent.heading)])
        side = np.array([-direction[1], direction[0]])
        if agent.kind == "person":
            radius = max(canvas.px(8), 0.3 * metre)
            reach = radius
            if agent.id in highlighted:
                canvas.circle((center[0], center[1]), radius * 2.1,
                              style.state_color(frame.state), thickness=canvas.px(2))
            canvas.circle((center[0], center[1]), radius + canvas.px(2), bg)
            canvas.circle((center[0], center[1]), radius, color)
            if agent.speed > 0.05:
                tip = center + direction * radius * 1.9
                canvas.lines([np.stack([center + direction * radius, tip])], color, canvas.px(3))
        else:
            length = max(canvas.px(30), 2.0 * agent.extent[0] * metre)
            half_w = max(canvas.px(7), agent.extent[1] * metre)
            reach = length / 2.0
            glyph = np.stack([center + direction * length / 2.0,
                              center - direction * length / 2.0 + side * half_w,
                              center - direction * length / 4.0,
                              center - direction * length / 2.0 - side * half_w])
            if agent.id in highlighted:
                canvas.circle((center[0], center[1]), length * 0.78,
                              style.state_color(frame.state), thickness=canvas.px(2))
            canvas.lines([glyph], bg, canvas.px(5), closed=True)
            canvas.polygon(glyph, color)
        if style.labels and agent.role == "scripted":
            text = _chip_text(agent)
            tw, _ = canvas.text_size(text, font, bold=True)
            cw, ch = tw + 2 * canvas.px(8), canvas.px(22, 13)
            x = center[0] + reach * 0.75 + canvas.px(8)
            y = center[1] - reach * 0.75 - canvas.px(8) - ch
            x = min(max(x, canvas.px(6)), width - cw - canvas.px(6))
            y = min(max(y, canvas.px(6)), height - ch - canvas.px(6))
            _draw_chip(canvas, (x, y, x + cw, y + ch), text, color)

    pad = canvas.px(28)
    if style.badge:
        _draw_badge(canvas, width - pad, pad, frame.state, align_right=True)
    if timeline is not None and style.timeline:
        lanes_h = 2 * canvas.px(6, 3) + canvas.px(5, 2)
        bar = float(to_px([[5.0, 0.0]])[0][0] - to_px([[0.0, 0.0]])[0][0])
        _draw_timeline(canvas, timeline, frame.t, pad, width - pad - bar - canvas.px(28),
                       height - pad - lanes_h)
    return out

A pole-height pinhole camera at the testbench camera position looks at the crosswalk over an analytic street backdrop, with agents placed from the scenario paths. Writes demo_view.png (the camera view with the HUD), demo_bev.png, demo_still.png (split layout), demo_fisheye.png when the fisheye module is available, and demo.mp4. Returns the paths under files together with the timeline of the scenario.
