docs.title: Detection and localisation uncertainty
docs.text: The testbench starts from exact scripted positions and degrades them before the decision pipeline sees them: a bounding-box localisation error, missed detections, and camera latency. This page documents the first two and the tracker that sits between them and the pipeline. Latency has its own page under experiments.

docs.title: Order of operations in one simulated frame
docs.text:
simulate_scenario does the following for every agent at every frame:

  1. If a recall value and a random generator were passed (the Monte Carlo mode), decide whether the detection is missed. The recall is looked up from the agent's projected bounding-box area.
  2. If the error model is on, replace the true position with the position that the bounding-box bottom-centre back-projects to. See perception.
  3. Push the frame's detections through the latency buffer.
  4. Update the ground-plane tracker, which fills in missed detections by prediction.
  5. Convert to camera-relative coordinates and call the decision pipeline.

--compare and the default run use steps 2, 4 and 5 only, so their output is the same on every run. Missed detections enter with --monte-carlo.

docs.title: Detector performance parameters
docs.text:
DetectionParams is a pair of average precision and average recall. SizedDetectionParams.for_area(bbox_area_px) returns the pair for a box of a given pixel area, measured at detector input scale (the area in the crop times (1280 / 3840)^2):

  • with an ar_curve loaded from an evaluation cache, recall is interpolated linearly over the curve's bin centres and precision is scaled by the same ratio;
  • with per-size values only, it uses the COCO bins: small below 32² = 1024 px², medium below 96² = 9216 px², large above;
  • with neither, it returns the overall values.

UncertaintyParams bundles the per-class parameters with the constants of the position model. The defaults are commented in the code as coming from the fisheye_1280 model evaluated on fisheye-augmented COCO.

Field Default Unit Meaning pedestrian AP 0.678, AR 0.755 Used for person agents. cyclist AP 0.657, AR 0.747 Used for bike agents. vehicle AP 0.706, AR 0.765 Used for every other class. bev_angular_error_deg 5.0 degrees Angular error assumed for the ground projection. kf_std_weight_pos 0.05 Position noise weight of the tracker's filter. kf_std_weight_vel 0.00625 Velocity noise weight. kf_max_lost 30 frames Frames a track may stay lost. kf_iou_threshold 0.2 Association threshold. fps 30 frames/s Frame rate. latency_ms 19.0 ms Nominal processing latency.

docs.title: Loading measured values
docs.text:
tools/eval_models.py evaluates one or more YOLO models and caches per-class results in eval_cache.json. Pass the cache to the testbench to replace the defaults:

python tools/eval_models.py --models yolo11x.pt --data cocoaug.yaml
python decision_testbench.py --monte-carlo --eval-cache eval_cache.json --eval-model yolo11x

load_uncertainty_from_cache reads the merged groups pedestrian, cyclist and vehicle of the chosen model, with keys ap5095, recall, per_size and ar_curve. Without --eval-model it takes the first model in the file. If the file does not exist it returns None and the defaults stay.

docs.title: Detection failure models
docs.text:
A failure model decides, per agent and per frame, whether a detection is missed, given the recall for that agent. FAILURE_MODELS maps the --failure-model choices to classes.

--failure-model Class Behaviour iid (default) IIDFailureModel Each frame is missed independently with probability 1 - AR. gilbert GilbertFailureModel A two-state Markov chain per agent produces runs of consecutive misses.

The Gilbert model has a detected state and a missed state. With mean burst length B (--burst-length, default 3.0 frames):

r = 1 / B                  # P(missed -> detected), recovery
p = (1 - AR) * r / AR      # P(detected -> missed), miss onset

The stationary miss rate p / (p + r) equals 1 - AR, so both models miss the same share of frames on average and differ in how the misses cluster. A burst length of 1.0 is close to the independent model. The chain state is kept per agent id and cleared between scenarios.

python decision_testbench.py --monte-carlo --mc-trials 50
python decision_testbench.py --monte-carlo --failure-model gilbert --burst-length 3

Bursts matter because the tracker and the cyclist memory both bridge short gaps. Independent misses at the same average rate are mostly bridged; a long run of misses on the cyclist is what delays an alert.

docs.title: Position uncertainty
docs.text:
compute_position_uncertainty(cam, gx, gy, obj, unc) estimates the standard deviation of a ground position at a given location from three terms and combines them as a root sum of squares:

Key Term sigma_yolo Box localisation: box size times (1 - AP) / (1 + AP), converted to metres with distance / f. sigma_bev Ground projection: distance * tan(bev_angular_error_deg). sigma_kf Tracker filter: kf_std_weight_pos times the box height, converted to metres. sigma_total Root sum of squares of the three. vel_std_world Velocity standard deviation in m/s.

The box size comes from projected_bbox_area, which projects the eight corners of the object's 3D box through the fisheye model and returns 0 when no corner is on the sensor.

docs.title: The ground-plane tracker
docs.text:
GroundPlaneTracker(track_buffer=30, match_radius=3.0) mirrors the tracker of the deployed bridge. Per frame it:

  1. moves every existing track forward by its velocity;
  2. matches detections to tracks of the same type by greedy nearest neighbour within match_radius metres;
  3. starts a new track for each unmatched detection;
  4. deletes tracks that have gone more than track_buffer frames without a detection;
  5. returns all live tracks, including the ones it only predicted.

Velocity and acceleration are exponential moving averages with weight 0.5. simulate_scenario builds the tracker with track_buffer=fps, one second of persistence. forecast(agents, n_frames, order) extrapolates positions with constant velocity (order=1) or constant acceleration (order=2) and is used for latency compensation.

docs.title: Effect of the localisation error
docs.text:
--no-bbox-noise feeds the pipeline the exact scripted positions. Totals over the 24 conformance scenarios with and without the error model:

python decision_testbench.py --compare
python decision_testbench.py --no-bbox-noise --compare
Configuration Sensitivity, with error Specificity, with error Sensitivity, exact positions Specificity, exact positions default 93.3% 92.3% 91.9% 92.5% conservative 77.1% 92.6% 75.9% 91.9% proximity_only 56.1% 97.4% 54.1% 97.0% speed_adaptive 93.1% 91.8% 92.2% 91.8% baseline_distance_only 57.8% 70.2% 54.7% 71.0% baseline_naive_closing 93.4% 90.4% 91.9% 90.8% baseline_ttc 84.3% 96.4% 84.0% 96.5%

For the default configuration the frame counts move from 1209 true positives and 361 false positives with exact positions to 1228 and 370 with the error model. The shift is small against the gaps between configurations, and the ranking of the decision rules is the same in both columns.
